title: Ireland – Construction work – 14 Tullyglass Hill
description: Corlann Clare invites tenders from suitably experienced building contractors for the extension and refurbishment of an existing single-storey dwelling at 14 Tullyglass Hill, Shannon, Co. Clare, V14 KH42. The works comprise a new single-storey extension of approximately 45 m² and the full refurbishment and upgrade of the existing house. The main elements are: • Demolition and strip-out: demolition of the existing lean-to structure on the east side; removal of the glazed courtyard roof, chimney stack, oil boiler and oil tank; full internal strip-out of finishes, ceilings, fittings, sanitaryware, and heating, plumbing and electrical installations. • New extension: 225 mm solid blockwork on a raft foundation to the Structural Engineer's design, with a certified external wall insulation and render system, and an insulated warm-deck flat roof. • Existing house: replacement of all windows and external doors; new and altered openings with steel beams and lintels; removal and alteration of internal walls; upgrade of all existing flat roofs to warm-deck construction; a new solid warm-deck roof with rooflights over the courtyard; rebuilt rooflight upstand walls; render repairs and redecoration; new fascias, gutters and downpipes. • Internal fit-out: new internal layout including WC and shower rooms, a widened stair and a new platform lift; FD30 fire door sets with closers and electromagnetic hold-open devices; fire-rated glazing; automatic opening smoke vents linked to a fire alarm system; [new heating, ventilation and electrical installations to the Specification]. • External works: widened entrance and tarmac driveway; new gently sloped footpaths and a level landing at a relocated main entrance on the west elevation; new and rebuilt retaining walls; new patio; replacement of asewer lines, installation of new manholes; new surface water drainage; tree removal and reinstatement of landscaping.

description: Stichting IMN past de Europese openbare aanbestedingsprocedure toe conform de Aanbestedingswet 2012. In 117 rayons is eerder dit jaar door een onderhandelingsprocedure een Bergingsovereenkomst 2026 - 2031 tot stand gekomen. De nu voorliggende aanbesteding heeft betrekking op de 99 rayons waarin nog geen bergingsovereenkomst werd gesloten. De rayons waar het om gaat zijn opgesomd in de Rayonlijst 2027 - 2031 (zie 1.3 Aanbestedingsleidraad). Onderwerp van aanbesteding is de Bergingsovereenkomst 2027 - 2031. Deze is, afgezien van de looptijd, identiek aan de in 117 rayons al tot stand gekomen Bergingsovereenkomst 2026 - 2031. Ieder aan te besteden rayon geldt als een zelfstandige opdracht en is onderwerp van een zelfstandige aanbestedingsprocedure. De gunningsbeslissingen in elk rayon zijn onafhankelijk van elkaar behoudens het gestelde in paragraaf 7.3. Dit betekent dat Stichting IMN voor ieder rayon kan besluiten om, als de omstandigheden daarnaar zijn, de aanbesteding in te trekken. De aanbesteding heeft uitsluitend betrekking op de in de Rayonlijst 2027 - 2031 vermelde rayons. (https://www.stichtingimn.nl/rayons.php). De nu voorliggende aanbesteding heeft betrekking op de 99 rayons.

title: OPEN, INSPECT, REPORT AND REPAIR HUB, STBD
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the FAR Overhaul Part 12 and as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation 70ZU0127Q20023 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. Full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. The U.S. Coast Guard, Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC) intends to award a Firm Fixed Price Purchase Order. No down payments or advanced payments will be made to the awarded vendor. Award will be made on a Best Value Basis as result of this synopsis/solicitation. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, which if timely received, shall be considered by this agency. description: The U.S. Department of Agriculture, U.S. Forest Service, Law Enforcement and Investigations program, Region 25 Fleet Management Office, Subunit 8, intends to restrict competition and award a contract for the final-stage upfit of one Government-furnished Chevrolet Silverado PPV law-enforcement vehicle, Equipment No. 5138. The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, transportation, installation, programming, integration, testing, and related services necessary to complete the law-enforcement K-9 vehicle upfit in accordance with the Government�s Statement of Work and applicable Forest Service requirements. The requirement includes, as applicable: Pickup and return of the Government-furnished vehicle; K-9 containment, transport, ventilation, heat-alert, and deployment systems; Integration and programming of emergency lighting and related controls; Interior task lighting and fire extinguisher installation; Firearms-storage equipment; Vehicle striping and graphics; Window tint; Installation and testing of Government-furnished telematics equipment; Printer-armrest and related power/data provisions; Keyboard and computer-mounting equipment; Radio faceplates and portable-radio charger equipment; Brush guard installation; and Inspection, functional testing, correction of deficiencies, and final acceptance. The completed vehicle must support Forest Service law-enforcement operations, including officer safety, K-9 transport and deployment, emergency response, secure equipment storage, communications support, and related operational requirements. All installed equipment must remain compatible with the vehicle�s original equipment manufacturer systems, safety systems, electrical architecture, airbags, restraints, diagnostics, sensors, and applicable warranty requirements. The Government-furnished vehicle will be available for pickup and will be returned to: USDA Forest Service WO Law Enforcement and Investigations, Subunit 8 6425 Lakeover Road, Suite A Jackson, Mississippi 39213 Upfitting, installation, integration, programming, testing, and secure storage will be performed at the contractor�s secure facility. The contractor�s facility must be located within 300 miles of the Government pickup location, unless the contractor provides transportation of the vehicle at the contractor�s expense. The contractor is responsible for protecting the Government vehicle and Government-furnished equipment while in its possession. Based on the market research documented in the acquisition file, the Government intends to restrict competition and consider an award to Dana Safety Supply, Inc., UEI FDNXL5D5KUF3, because the company reportedly has the required equipment available and can meet the Government�s required schedule. The Government is seeking information from responsible sources that believe they can provide all required equipment and services, meet the technical requirements, and complete the work within the required timeframe (date of award- 02/28/2027). Interested sources shall submit a capability statement addressing: Experience performing law-enforcement, emergency-response, K-9, or comparable vehicle upfits; Ability to furnish and install the equipment identified in the Statement of Work; Availability of required equipment and materials; Ability to meet the Government�s required schedule; Experience integrating equipment with Chevrolet PPV or comparable police-vehicle platforms; Ability to maintain a secure facility and use properly vetted personnel; Relevant past performance; and Legal business name, address, point of contact, telephone number, email address, UEI, and applicable NAICS code. Capability statements shall be submitted electronically to Michael J. Wheelock no later than Wednesday, November 25, 2026 at 10:00A.M. EST . Responses shall reference Requisition No. 1178993. This notice is not a request for quotations and does not constitute a solicitation. No solicitation is currently available. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with submitting information. The Government may consider information received in response to this notice before making a final acquisition decision. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

title: F014--TREE REMOVAL VAMC MARTINSBURG
description: Tree Removal Services - Safety Mitigation at VAMC Martinsburg� Notice Type� Sources Sought / Market Research� NAICS Code� 561730 - Landscaping Services� Place of Performance� VAMC Martinsburg, 510 Butler Avenue, Martinsburg, WV 25405� Response Due� November 25th at 10am EST Submission Email� Cassie.white@va.gov 1. Purpose� The Department of Veterans Affairs is conducting market research to identify qualified businesses capable of providing professional tree removal services at the Martinsburg VA Medical Center. The Government seeks information regarding industry capability, business size and socioeconomic status, relevant experience, and anticipated availability. The information received may be used to support acquisition strategy and determine whether a future requirement may be suitable for a small business set-aside or another procurement approach.� 2. Requirement Overview� The anticipated requirement is for a contractor to furnish all labor, supervision, materials, tools, equipment, transportation, traffic and pedestrian controls, and services necessary to remove six designated declining oak trees near the front entrance of the medical center campus.� Remove six VA-designated declining oak trees using professional tree-removal and rigging methods.� Cut each stump as close to grade as safely and reasonably practicable, not to exceed approximately six inches above surrounding grade unless otherwise directed. Stump grinding and stump/FboNotice removal are excluded.� Remove all branches, logs, leaves, chips, and other debris from VA property and lawfully dispose of the material off site.� Protect buildings, sidewalks, roadways, curbs, landscaping, utilities, signs, vehicles, and other Government property.� Maintain safe medical center access and coordinate any temporary restrictions or closures with the VA point of contact.� Establish appropriate work zones, exclusion zones, warning devices, barricades, spotters, and pedestrian/vehicle controls.� Perform the work in accordance with applicable OSHA requirements and applicable ANSI Z133 and ANSI A300 standards.� Coordinate scheduling and approved work hours to minimize disruption to medical center operations.� 3. Contractor Qualifications� Professional tree-care operations performed under the direction of qualified personnel, with a certified arborist and/or appropriately licensed tree expert available as applicable.� All licenses, permits, certifications, insurance, and workers compensation coverage required by Federal, State, and local law maintained throughout performance.� Ability to provide documentation of applicable certifications and insurance upon request.� Capability to safely perform work in an active medical center environment while protecting patients, visitors, staff, vehicles, and property.� 4. Requested Information� Interested parties should submit a concise capability statement addressing each item below. Responses should be sufficiently detailed for the Government to assess capability, but should not include pricing unless specifically identified as a rough-order-of-magnitude estimate.� Item� Requested response information� 1� Company name, physical address, website, and primary point of contact, including name, title, telephone number, and email address.� 2� Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and confirmation of active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov).� 3� Business size under NAICS 561730 and all applicable socioeconomic categories, such as small business, SDVOSB, VOSB, HUBZone, WOSB/EDWOSB, or 8(a). For VA veteran-owned categories, state current SBA VetCert status.� 4� A narrative describing the company s technical approach and ability to provide all personnel, equipment, rigging, traffic controls, debris removal, and supervision required.� 5� Relevant experience from up to three comparable projects completed within the past five years. Include customer, location, scope, approximate contract value, period of performance, and customer point of contact if releasable.� 6� Applicable arborist credentials, tree-expert licenses, safety qualifications, and typical insurance coverage.� 7� Estimated mobilization lead time and the approximate number of workdays needed to complete the requirement after site access and scheduling are coordinated.� 8� Whether the company intends to perform as the prime contractor and the approximate percentage of work expected to be self-performed.� 9� Any recommended contract type, commercial terms, industry practices, site information, or revisions that would improve competition, safety, scheduling, or performance.� 10� Whether a site visit would be necessary to prepare a reliable quotation, and any specific information the Government should make available for that visit.� 11� Optional: a nonbinding rough-order-of-magnitude price range, clearly identified as budgetary market research information only.� 5. Response Instructions� Submit responses electronically to the email address listed above by the stated response deadline.� Use the subject line: RFI Response - Tree Removal Services - NAICS 561730 - [Company Name]. � Limit the response to 10 pages, excluding a cover page and supporting certifications.� Provide responses in searchable PDF or Microsoft Word format.� Do not submit proprietary information unless it is clearly marked. The Government may use support contractors to assist with market research, subject to appropriate safeguards.� Questions regarding this RFI should be submitted in writing to the contracting office contact identified in the notice.� 6. Additional Information� The Government may contact respondents for clarification or additional market research. Participation in this RFI is voluntary and is not required to compete in any future solicitation. The Government is under no obligation to issue a solicitation or award a contract as a result of this notice. Any future solicitation will be issued separately and will govern the requirement.� 7. Draft Performance Summary� The anticipated place of performance is the front entrance area of VAMC Martinsburg, 510 Butler Avenue, Martinsburg, West Virginia 25405. The VA will identify the six trees and provide reasonable access. The period of performance and work schedule will be established in a future solicitation or award document. Contractor access, temporary closures, and impacts to emergency routes or entrances must be coordinated and approved in advance.� 8. Contracting Office Information� Contracting Officer- Cassie White Email- cassie.white@va.gov

title: Q301-- FISH TECH Testing
description: THIS NOTICE IS FOR PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY. THE GOVERNMENT DOES NOT INTEND TO AWARD A CONTRACT ON THE BASIS OF THE SOURCE SOUGHT OR REIMBURSE ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH THE PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO SOURCES SOUGHT. This is a SOURCES SOUGHT for the Richmond VA Medical Center located at 1201 Broad Rock Blvd, Richmond, VA 23249 VA 23249. Seeking market research for FISH Tech lab testing. If a solicitation is issued, the Government will do so in accordance with Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) (FAC 2026-01), effective 03/2026. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) number is 621511. The NAICS size is $41.5 million. Any contractor that believes they are capable and desires to claim preference for small business status must be registered with the SBA at http://web.sba.gov/pro-net/ and meet the requirements of FAR 19.102. Any contractor that believes they are capable and desires to claim preference for veteran-owned small business status must be registered with the VIP at https://sba.va.gov/ as an SDVOSB or VOSB. A Contractor that proposes to provide a supply that is not manufactured by their organization (nonmanufacturer) shall meet the requirements of FAR 19.102(f). The contractor shall provide testing as outlined in this SOW (see test menu). Testing services shall be available within 30 days of contract award. For laboratory samples, Richmond VAMC will provide either an electronic generated patient worklist or contractor provided requisition form containing at a minimum the patient s full name, date of birth (second identifier), hospital identification number, tests to be performed, sample collection date/time, ordering provider, and sample type. For specialized testing, the VAMC will provide a brief clinical history only when necessary. Requisitions may be electronic. Description: CPT codes 80000-90000 and U0001-U1000 shall be included as well as generic codes when new tests are implemented. New tests or products not identified in the contract may be added with the permission of the Contracting Officer (CO). General Information: The Contractor Laboratory shall: Perform testing services entirely upon their premises. Accept VA generated manifests as patient test requisitions. Accept the unique facility National Provider Identifier (NPI) number and not require an NPI for each individual ordering practitioner. Perform analytical testing for VAMC patients for the tests defined in the test menu included in this SOW. The Contractor shall bill only for the tests specified in the request sent by the VAMC Laboratory service. Provide a reference test manual, and report of analytical test results and consultative services as required, assimilating the full scope of its laboratory operations. Provide VAMC with appropriate laboratory supplies not customarily utilized by the VAMC. These supplies are to be used by the VAMC only in connection with specimens being sent for testing to the contractor. Furnish all supplies required for specimen transport, including but not limited to laboratory test request forms or requisitions, specimen shipping containers, special handling instructions, and transportation envelopes or shipping packs with tracking capability. Provide all transportation and shipping necessary to ensure the safe, timely, and compliant delivery of specimens from Richmond VAMC to the contractor s laboratory facility. Timely transportation is specimen receipt in the contractor lab within 24 hours of departure from Richmond VAMC The contractor shall provide Saturday pickup availability as needed by Richmond VAMC Carry out its functions hereunder in full compliance with all local, state, and federal laws or regulations. Provide all test result reports/consults in less than 5 days of receiving the sample, except for bone marrow flow cytometry cases Test results for bone marrow flow cytometry cases shall be available within 24 hours of receipt to the contractor laboratory Provide complete processed samples as defined in the test menu. Return all embedded tissue within 5 days of completing sample processing and reporting. Provide a consultation/professional interpretation when requested on select cases. Results shall include all applicable information, not limited to: Patient s full name Patient s date of birth Patient s full social security number or unique VAMC hospital identification number Ordering Physician s name Date/time of specimen collection, when available Date/time test completed Test(s) ordered Test result(s) Flagged abnormal results - if applicable Type of specimen/source Any additional comments related to test provided by ordering physician, if applicable Unsatisfactory specimens shall be reported regarding unsuitability for testing VAMC Lab accession number, if supplied VAMC submitting facility name Patient location- if supplied Date/time specimen receipt Abnormal intervals/Toxic & therapeutic ranges - if applicable Any other information the laboratory has that may indicate a questionable validity of test results. VAMC facility account number Contractor accession number Contractor address Contractor Department of Health and Human Services Clinical Laboratory Improvement Act of 1988 (CLIA) number Reference intervals- if applicable Testing laboratory name Consult with VAMC on test results by telephone, as needed. Provide an online portal that allows VAMC pathologist(s) to retrieve processed specimen technical data and create their professional interpretation on the contractor s portal. Patient reports shall be available for download from contractor portal in pdf format. Portal shall be secure and accessible on VA network Portal shall be available to other VAMC employees as designated by the COR of the contract Provide training, at no additional charge, for pathologist(s) to retrieve processed specimen data and create interpretation report on the contractors portal and lab staff to download completed reports. Allow add on markers for FISH testing after initial results are received. This should include but is not limited to the ability to add RPNI, MECOM, ETV6, 17p-, +19 to the MDS Standard FISH panel. Provide a printed or electronic Laboratory Manual containing the following information: Testing methodology for a test must be defined in the laboratory user s manual Department hours of operation Accreditation Technical Staff Service Departments (Method of contacting, phone numbers, hours of availability) Quality Assurance Information Billing Procedures & fee schedules for services provided Procedures and criteria for phoning reports and other important information Report forms Provide telephone number(s) and contact person(s) to be used by the VAMC to make specimen problem inquiries and problem solving on weekdays. *NOTE: Also include names and telephone number(s) of Technical Directors and Pathologists available for consultation. Maintain the minimum acceptable service, reporting systems, and quality control as specified herein. Immediate (within 24 hours) notification shall be given to VA upon adverse action by a regulatory agency. Assign a specific local account representative. Advise VAMC facility of any planned changes in methodology, procedure, or reference ranges at least 14 days prior to changes. In the event that two-week notification is not possible due to emergency, contractor shall notify Richmond VAMC as soon as possible. Not release patient s records that include test results to any person other than the ordering healthcare provider or VA Pathology and Laboratory Medicine staff member. All member records shall be treated as confidential to comply with all state and federal laws regarding the confidentiality of patient s records. This provision shall survive termination of the resulting contract award. Certify and ensure that all employees, officers, or agents do not use Protected Health Information received from any VAMC site that would constitute a violation of any applicable provision in standards set forth in HIPA

title: U006--VR&E Self-Employment Services RFI
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) SUBJECT Exploring the Feasibility of VA Partnering with Industry to Ready Disabled Veterans for Self-Employment (i.e., entrepreneurship; small business ownership) 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA), is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) for Veteran Readiness & Employment (VR&E) Self-Employment Services. The information provided in response to this request may be used by VBA in developing its acquisition strategy and refining the Performance Work Statement (PWS). THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI or otherwise pay for the information requested. Responses will be treated as information only and not as a proposal. There is no obligation for the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI. In accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Subpart 15.101(c)(2), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. 2.0 BACKGROUND VBA s VR&E Service, pursuant to Title 38 United States Code Chapter 31 (see Section 3100), provides to eligible Veterans with compensable service-connected disabilities all services and assistance necessary to enable them to achieve maximum independence in daily living and, to the maximum extent feasible, to become employable and to obtain and maintain suitable employment. After achieving the degree of rehabilitation needed to become suitably employed, VR&E is expected to assist Veterans in the pursuit of suitable employment. One such avenue through which VR&E assists is utilizing VR&E s Self-Employment Track, which is intended to assist eligible Veterans in achieving their vocational goals in entrepreneurship and business ownership. Services include the following: Developing and strengthening a business plan Training in small-business operations, marketing, finances, etc. Assessing the feasibility of implementing such a business plan Obtaining (through loans or grants) the resources necessary to implement a business plan and incorporate the business such as securing loans Purchasing of equipment, acquiring initial stocks and supplies, etc. Specialized expertise and/or support to assist Veterans interested in self-employment includes, but is not limited to, knowledge of local/state/federal laws associated with starting a business;� market research/analysis both from the perspective of assessing viability of the prospective business in the job market and through the lens of purchasing subject matter expertise and purchasing equipment/supplies; and� potential screening or other assessment tools for specialized job markets (i.e. ability to run background checks and/or credit checks to assess criminal history, driving records, substance use/abuse, financial/credit/tax history, education, etc.). Further, VA recognizes that achieving successful self-employment outcomes often requires specialized expertise beyond traditional vocational rehabilitation services. Veterans pursuing entrepreneurship may need support with business planning, feasibility analysis, market research, financial literacy, regulatory compliance, business startup requirements, mentorship, and access to entrepreneurial networks and resources. Self-employment cases frequently involve complex business considerations that require specialized knowledge, individualized assessments, and coordination with public and private sector resources. Veterans may require assistance evaluating business viability, developing comprehensive business plans, understanding applicable licensing and regulatory requirements, conducting market and financial analyses, identifying startup resource needs, and building the skills necessary to successfully operate a small business. These needs often require tailored, ongoing guidance throughout the planning and launch process. VA is seeking information on how experienced industry partners can supplement existing VR&E services by providing subject matter expertise, structured entrepreneurial training, business feasibility assessments, market research capabilities, business financial planning and analysis (i.e., financial projections, startup cost estimates, cash flow planning, and capital requirements), and access to established business support networks. Such services may help Veterans make informed business decisions, evaluate and strengthen the viability of proposed business ventures, develop stronger business plans, and access the expertise and resources needed to successfully launch and sustain a small business. Accordingly, VA requests information from organizations with demonstrated experience providing entrepreneur and small business support services, including business advisory services, training, business feasibility and market assessments, entrepreneurial training, startup incubation, financial planning, and other related support services. The goal is to identify potential partnership approaches that can enhance VA's ability to assist Veterans with service-connected disabilities in evaluating business concepts, developing viable business plans, preparing for business ownership, and successfully launching and sustaining small businesses 3.0 INFORMATION SOUGHT The Government is seeking the following information from vendors responding to this RFI: Organization and Contact Information, specifically: Name of Organization Addresses for Primary Locations of Operation Points of Contact (available for follow-up discussions) Phone Numbers and Email Addresses for Points of Contact Business Size and Socioeconomic Status Answers to List of Questions (See Section 5.0 of this RFI) Past Performance (if applicable) describing how your organization: has supported entrepreneurs in exploring, planning, and starting small business enterprises prepared entrepreneurs for operating small business enterprises with training, apprenticeships, mentorships, and similar educational ventures 4.0 SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Please submit responses to the Contracting Officer, Edward Bradford, via email Edward.Bradford@va.gov no later than November 25, 2026. Responses shall not exceed 10 pages total and shall be prepared in Times New Roman, 12-point font, with 1-inch margins. 5.0 LIST OF QUESTIONS Please provide information regarding proposed joint ventures, teaming arrangements, or strategic alliances you believe would be beneficial in supporting the needs of Veterans pursuing self-employment outlined in the background section of this document. Please describe your organization s expertise in providing business planning, self-employment, entrepreneurship, small business operations, and startup incubation services. Please describe how your organization would prepare for and respond to referrals issued by VR&E, specifically the timelines for contacting Veterans participating in the Self-Employment Track and the type of services your organization would provide throughout the engagement. Please describe your organization s service delivery model, including how services would be documented and how progress, milestones, and outcomes would be communicated to VA. On average, how many full-time equivalent (FTE) business consultants, entrepreneurship specialists, or small business advisors are employed by your company? How long has your company been providing self-employment, entrepreneurship development, small business consulting, or related business advisory services? Please provide the qualifications, certifications, or specialized training your business consultants possess related to entrepreneurship? Please describe your experience developing business plans, feasibility studies, and financial projections. title: Automated Digital Flatbed Cutting and Routing Equipment
description: 1.0 DESCRIPTION The 355th Contracting Squadron is conducting market research to identify interested and capable businesses that can provide commercial automated digital flatbed cutting and routing equipment, Colex Sharpcut Pro or Equal, meeting the requirements described in Section 2.0 of this notice and in Attachment 1 - Vendor Capability Questionnaire. This Sources Sought Notice is for market research purposes only and is not a solicitation. 2.0 REQUIREMENT SUMMARY Item: Two automated digital flatbed cutting and routing systems, Colex Sharpcut Pro or Equal, as further described in Attachment 1. System 1: Minimum active cutting area of 120 inches by 60 inches, including automated board feeding with pallet-table or equivalent continuous-loading capability. System 2: Minimum active cutting area of 80 inches by 124 inches. Capabilities: Motorized conveyor beds; vacuum hold-down; cutting, routing, creasing, and marking for rigid and flexible packaging and preservation materials; and compatible or interoperable tooling and software/workflow between both systems. Services: Turnkey delivery, installation, configuration, and three days of on-site operator training for each system. The vendor shall identify the organization proposed to perform installation and training and its relationship to the OEM. Warranty and support: At least one year of warranty for non-consumable parts and labor, plus one year of telephone or remote technical support. Delivery Terms: F.O.B. Destination to Davis-Monthan AFB, Arizona 85707. NAICS Code: 333248 - Other Industrial Machinery Manufacturing. PSC: 3610 - Printing, Duplicating, and Bookbinding Equipment. 3.0 RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS Interested and capable businesses must respond to this notice no later than Wednesday, November 25th 2026 at 8:00 AM MST (Tucson, AZ local time). Responses must be sent via email to the Contracting Officer; Patricia Murray, patricia.murray.6@us.af.mil Responses must include the following information: 1. Completed Attachment 1 - Vendor Capability Questionnaire. 2. Manufacturer product literature or a specification sheet for each proposed system. Product literature should provide sufficient detail for the Government to assess the proposed equipment against the requirements identified in Attachment 1. The completed questionnaire must identify the organization proposed to perform installation and training and indicate whether that organization is the OEM, an OEM-authorized provider, or another provider. No separate authorization documentation is requested with this Sources Sought response. 4.0 DISCLAIMER Information received in response to this notice may be used to inform the Government's acquisition strategy, including small business and competition determinations. The Government does not guarantee that a solicitation or award will result from this notice and will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparing or submitting a response to this notice.

title: Finland – Transport services (excl. Waste transport) – Kirjastoaineistojen logistiikka- ja kuljetuspalvelut
description: Hankinnan kohteena ovat kirjastoaineiston kuljetus- ja logistiikkapalvelut PIKI-kirjastoverkostolle. Hankinnan tavoitteena on varmistaa kirjastoaineiston tehokas, luotettava, laadukas ja kustannustehokas liikkuvuus seudullisesti. Kuljetuksia toteutetaan kohteesta riippuen eri palvelutasoin. Osa kirjastoista palvellaan päivittäin arkipäivisin, kun taas osaan kohteista kuljetuksia järjestetään 1-2 kertaa viikossa. Kuljetettavien laatikoiden määrä vaihtelee kohdekohtaisesti sekä päivä- että viikkotasolla, yksittäisistä laatikoista yli kymmeneen laatikkoon kuljetuskertaa kohden. Alustava kuljetusaikataulu on esitetty tarjouspyynnön liitteessä. Hankinta käsittää PIKI-kirjastoverkoston kirjastoaineistologistiikan kuljetus- ja siihen liittyvät palvelut. Palveluun sisältyvät kirjastoaineiston kuljetukset ensisijaisesti PIKI-kirjastojen pääkirjastojen välillä sekä aineiston käsittelyyn, lajitteluun ja logistiikan hallintaan liittyvät tehtävät. Hankinnan tarkempi sisältö, palvelutasovaatimukset, kuljetuskohteet, arvioidut volyymit, aikataulut, raportointivaatimukset sekä muut palvelun toteuttamiseen liittyvät ehdot on kuvattu tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä. Hankintaa ei ole jaettu erillisiin osa-alueisiin, koska hankinnan kohteena oleva palvelu muodostaa tarkoituksenmukaisen rajatun kokonaisuuden tehtävineen. Hankinnan tavoitteena on turvata kirjastoaineiston sujuva saatavuus asiakkaille sekä tukea kirjastoverkon tehokasta, laadukasta ja toimintavarmaa palvelutuotantoa koko sopimuskauden ajan. Sopimuskausi on 1.7.2027- 30.6.2031.

THE SOLICITATION NUMBER IS N6945027R0008, FOR THE DESIGN-BID-BUILD (DBB) CONSTRUCTION PROJECT P233 AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL TOWER AND FLIGHT SIMULATOR TRAINING FACILITY AT KEESLER AIR FORCE BASE (AFB), BILOXI, MISSISSIPPI PROJECT TITLE: DESIGN BID BUILD (DBB) CONSTRUCTION PROJECT, P233 AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL TOWER AND FLIGHT SIMULATOR TRAINING FACILITY AT KEESLER AIR FORCE BASE (AFB), BILOXI, MISSISSIPPI PSC: Y1BA (Construction of Air Traffic Control Towers) NAICS: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS OR AN INVITATION FOR BID. NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUESTS. No telephone calls will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. There is no bid package or solicitation currently available. In order to protect the procurement integrity of any future procurement that may arise from this announcement, information regarding the technical point of contact will not be given and no appointments for presentations will be made. Description: This acquisition may result in the award of a Design Bid Build (DBB) Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Construction contract of an Air Traffic Control Tower and Flight Simulator Training Facility at Keesler AFB, Mississippi. This project will construct a new Air Traffic Control Tower and adjacent Flight Simulator Facility. Project includes all utilities, site improvements, pavements, elevator, backup generator, and all necessary work for a complete and usable facility. Project will comply with Department of Defense Antiterrorism/Force Protection requirements per Unified Facilities Criteria 4-010-01 and Unified Facilities Criteria 3-600-01. A Bid Option is included for the demolition of Buildings 4209 and 4230, to include site grading and the installation of a security fence. Demolition in this bid option to only occur after the new Air Traffic Control Tower is complete. The estimated Period of Performance is 1,219 calendar days. The best value continuum source selection process to be used for this acquisition is the Best Value Tradeoff process as described in FAR 15.103-1. The Best Value Tradeoff process is appropriate and permits evaluation of proposals based on price competition, technical merit, confidence assessment and other factors; permits impartial and comprehensive evaluation of offeror proposals; permits discussions if necessary; and ensures selection of the source whose performance provides the best value to the Government. A sources sought notice was posted to sam.gov on October 27, 2026, requesting small business industry interest and capability statements. Based on responses from the notice it was determined that the requirement should be issued as Full and Open competition. The solicitation will be a negotiated DBB acquisition. Proposals will be solicited in a one-phase submission for a single solicitation. The solicitation will utilize source selection procedures, which require offerors to submit a technical proposal, past performance and experience information, and a price proposal for evaluation by the Government. Award will be made to the offeror whose total price and technical proposal offers the best value to the Government. Competition Requirements: Unrestricted basis, under full and open competition. Procurement Method: FAR Part 15, Contracting by Negotiation. Type of Contract: Firm-Fixed Price The NAICS code for this construction solicitation is 236220 with a size standard of $45,000,000. Project Magnitude is between $20,000,000 and $50,000,000. This is a new procurement. It does not replace an existing contract. No prior contract information exists. A Site Visit will be held for those offerors who choose to participate (exact date and time will be specified in the solicitation). Proposals will be due no earlier than 30 days after the solicitation is released (exact date and time will be specified in the solicitation). This will be an electronic solicitation, which can be downloaded from Sam.gov Opportunities at https://sam.gov/. The solicitation will be available at this site no earlier than 15 days after this pre-solicitation notice is posted. Offerors are responsible for checking the Sam.gov website for the solicitation and any subsequent amendments that may be issued. NO CONTRACT AWARD WILL BE MADE TO ANY CONTRACTOR THAT IS NOT REGISTERED OR IN THE PROCESS OF REGISTERING WITH THE SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM). PLEASE VISIT THE SAM WEBSITE AT https://www.sam.gov FOR INSTRUCTIONS ON HOW TO REGISTER.

title: J012--Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning, Kitchen Fire Suppression System Service, and Portable Fire Extinguisher Service
description: 1. Title: Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning, Kitchen Fire Suppression System Service, and Portable Fire Extinguisher Service 2. Background: Per NFPA 96, the new Food Services Center (Bldg. 211), and JLM dietetics are required to have their kitchen hoods cleaned semiannually due to limited grease use and/or limited meal service. The hoods for JLM, B170, and 202 require quarterly cleaning due to the heavy grease operations. During regular cleaning, the hood system must be inspected, tested and maintained. Per NFPA and regulatory requirements, kitchen fire suppression systems shall be inspected and serviced at a minimum of every 6 months to ensure proper operation and life safety compliance. Given that the kitchen fire suppression systems will be inspected, government is including the inspection, testing and maintenance of the portable fire extinguisher. Per NFPA and regulatory requirements, portable fire extinguishers shall be inspected, serviced, and hydrotested to ensure proper operation. 3. Purpose: The Network Contracting Office (NCO) 16, located at Galleria Financial Center, 5075 Westheimer Rd, Ste 750, Houston, TX 77030, hereby issues the following Sources Sought to Request Information (RFI) with the intent of determining the contractor interest, capabilities, qualifications of potential businesses and estimated industry pricing information for market research and estimated budgetary purpose for Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning, Kitchen Fire Suppression System Service, and Portable Fire Extinguisher Service 4. Requirement summary: The Government presently considers fire-protection equipment inspection, testing, preventive maintenance, recharge, hydrostatic testing, repair, authorized replacement, and restoration to be the predominant purpose of the integrated requirement. Accordingly, North American Industry Classification System code 811310 is proposed.� The anticipated requirement combines recurring commercial services at the John L. McClellan Memorial Veterans Hospital in Little Rock and the Eugene J. Towbin Healthcare Center in North Little Rock. The draft scope includes:� Quarterly and semiannual cleaning of identified commercial kitchen hoods, plenums, ducts, fans, dampers, and related exhaust-system components.� Semiannual inspection, testing, maintenance, tagging, and documentation for 10 wet-chemical kitchen fire suppression systems.� Inspection, maintenance, recharge, hydrostatic testing, repair, authorized replacement, pickup, return, tagging, and asset-level reporting for approximately 948 portable fire extinguishers across listed classes and locations.� Qualified personnel, manufacturer authorization when required, calibrated test equipment, safety controls, chemical and waste management, impairment coordination, incident reporting support, and digital service records.� A potential base period with four one-year option periods. The final contract structure and quantities have not been determined.� Respondents should address the ability to perform all three principal service areas as the prime contractor and identify any anticipated subcontracting or teaming arrangement. 5. Requested capability information: Interested parties should submit a concise capability statement, preferably no more than 10 pages excluding cover page and supporting certifications. Clearly identify proprietary information. Address each item below in the order listed.� Legal business name, physical address, website, and primary point of contact, including name, title, telephone number, and email address.� Unique Entity Identifier and Commercial and Government Entity code.� Business size under proposed North American Industry Classification System code 811310 and any recommended alternative code.� Socioeconomic status, including small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business, women-owned small business, economically disadvantaged women-owned small business, Historically Underutilized Business Zone small business, 8(a) participant, or small disadvantaged business. Identify current Small Business Administration VetCert status when claiming veteran-owned or service-disabled veteran-owned status.� Whether the respondent intends to perform as the prime contractor and the approximate percentage of work the respondent expects to perform with its own employees.� Capability to provide all required service areas at both campuses, including after-hours kitchen exhaust cleaning and normal-business-hours fire protection services.� Current qualifications and certifications relevant to National Fire Protection Association Standards 10, 17A, and 96; Underwriters Laboratories 300-listed systems; Ansul and PyroChem systems; kitchen exhaust cleaning; extinguisher maintenance; and hydrostatic testing. Identify whether credentials are held by the respondent or a proposed subcontractor.� At least two recent and relevant contracts or projects completed within the past five years. Include customer, contract or project identifier if releasable, period of performance, dollar magnitude or range, scope, locations, and customer point of contact if authorized.� Available staffing, mobilization timeframe, service radius, emergency or impairment response capability, and ability to maintain recurring schedules at both campuses.� Quality-control approach, asset tracking, service-report format, deficiency management, chain-of-custody controls, and ability to provide searchable Microsoft Excel or Portable Document Format reports.� Any contract vehicle available to the Government, including Federal Supply Schedule contract information, if applicable.� 6. Licenses, certifications, and technical qualifications: Respondents shall identify the licenses, certifications, manufacturer authorizations, and technical qualifications currently available to perform the draft requirement. A credential matrix is acceptable at the Sources Sought stage. Do not submit Social Security numbers, dates of birth, home addresses, or other unnecessary personal information. Current Arkansas Fire Protection Licensing Board company Certificate of Registration for portable fire-extinguisher systems and fixed fire-suppression systems. Current individual Arkansas licenses for proposed or available technicians covering portable fire extinguishers, fixed wet-chemical fire-suppression systems, and hydrostatic testing, as applicable to assigned work. Current Ansul and Pyro-Chem manufacturer-authorized distributor, service-provider, or technician documentation applicable to the installed system models. Identify any other manufacturer authorization available. International Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning Association Certified Exhaust Cleaning Specialist, Certified Exhaust Cleaning Technician, or an equivalent nationally recognized commercial kitchen exhaust-cleaning credential for the proposed crew leader or onsite supervisor. A Professional Exhaust Cleaning Technician designation should be identified as a designation rather than represented as a full certification. Current Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration Requalifier Identification Number approval for any facility that will inspect, test, mark, or requalify regulated cylinders. If this work will be subcontracted, identify the proposed testing facility and provide its approval information. Current Arkansas hydrostatic-testing license or certificate applicable to the cylinder classes and testing methods proposed. Current calibration certificates for pressure gauges, scales, hydrostatic-test equipment, electrical test instruments, and other measurement equipment whose accuracy affects inspection or acceptance. Relevant safety-training records, including lockout/tagout, hazard communication, personal protective equipment, fall protection or rooftop work, ladder or lift operation, respiratory protection when applicable, and spill response. Current certificate of general liability insurance and identification of workers compensation and automobile

title: APN-CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT SERVICES, MAINLAND BC INFRASTRUCTURE MODERNIZATION
description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR MAINLAND BRITISH COLUMBIA INFRASTRUCTURE MODERNIZATION PROGRAM (with security requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at Chilliwack, British Columbia and various range and training areas across Mainland BC. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. APN: 87908 Approximate Estimate: $125,000,000 Anticipated Posting: Winter 2027 Description: The Infrastructure Modernization Program at Chilliwack, British Columbia and various range and training areas across Mainland BC is focused on both recapitalization of existing assets and the development of new infrastructure and facilities where required. As part of this project, the Department of National Defence (DND) wishes to proceed with the renewal of systems which include civil, architectural, mechanical, electrical, and environmental elements to bring the assets to meet current and projected future requirements. This program will include planned phased work packages for implementation over ten (10) years while maintaining operations across Mainland BC. The purpose of this project is to retain the services of a contractor to provide construction management services of pre-construction and construction phases.  Major construction services are expected to include activities such as interior/exterior demolition in the presence of hazardous materials, interior renovations, exterior envelope work, electrical, mechanical, civil, structural and new infrastructure. 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). 4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a proposal.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Contractors that do not submit a proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Theresa Tran Coordinator, Contract Services Defence Construction Canada (604) 832 8373 theresa.tran@dcc-cdc.gc.ca 7. Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: Provision of BMS System MEICA-BMS-01
description: The scope of works includes a two-stage delivery approach covering the complete design, supply, configuration, integration, testing and installation of the Building Management System for Canley Brook, Burton Green and Stoneleigh Pumping Stations under the HS2 N1/N2 MEICA works. The centralised system at each location shall comprise of a dedicated BMS panel with dual-redundant PLCs, HMIs, remote interface enclosures and a dedicated BMS LAN, and distributed interface enclosures located within the relevant plant rooms to facilitate communications between plant systems and provide connectivity to the HS2 Network Integrated Control Centre (NICC). The BMS shall integrate the mechanical and electrical building services, providing monitoring, control, alarm management, and operator interfaces for the pumping stations and portal building. The system shall be designed in accordance with the project control strategy and applicable HS2 technical standards while coordinating with interfacing subcontractors to ensure seamless integration of all connected systems. The proposed BMS shall provide monitoring, control, alarms and graphical visualisation for HVAC, LV distribution and metering, UPS, lighting, fire alarms, public health services, pumped drainage and disabled toilet alarms. The scope also includes reviewing design inputs, updating the Functional Design Specification and generic drawings, and coordinating all interfaces required for full mechanical and electrical system integration. Sella Controls will also assess the cyber security risks associated with the BMS system. Additional information: Please review the Scope of work and drawings for the works.

The CDR requires the Contractor to explain, in writing, the cause of the unsatisfactory performance, how performance will be returned to acceptable standards, and how reoccurrence of the problem will be prevented in the future. Contracting Officer (CO): The individual with the authority to enter into, administer, and/or terminate contracts. The CO is the exclusive Government official authorized to execute changes and deviations or variations in the contract. Contracting Officer's Technical Representative (COTR) : A Government representative, designated in writing by the Contracting Officer, to be responsible for quality assurance, inspection, surveillance, documentation and acceptance of the Contractor's performance. A copy of the letter of designation will be provided to the Contractor. Preventive Maintenance (PM): Services which are periodic in nature and are required to maintain the equipment in such condition that it may be operated in accordance with its intended design and functional capacity with minimal incidence of malfunction or inoperative conditions. To clean, lubricate, calibrate, and test the equipment and/or instrument to the operating condition defined in the manufacturer s specifications. Repair Cost Estimate: The Contractors estimated cost (for parts, labor and freight) to repair a system according to manufactures' specifications and requirements. title: FMC Carswell 2 QTR FY27 Halal Meal Solicitation
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul FAR Subpart 12.2, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The solicitation number is 15B50527Q00000007 and is issued as a Request for Quote (RFQ). This Solicitation is for 2nd Qtr. FY27 Halal Meals Solicitation. The solicitation document, incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Revolutionary FAR Overhaul issuance date May 2, 2025. This solicitation is issued as Total small business set-aside. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 311999 with a small business size standard of 700.00 employees. FOB Destination shall be to: FMC Carswell Food Service Department 1200 Meandering Road, Fort Worth, Texas 76114. Items will be awarded individually. More than one item may be awarded to one offeror/contractor. Award will be given to the offeror whose bid/quote conforms to the requirements and is determined to provide the best value to the Government. The following are the evaluation factors that will be used to evaluate each offeror are price, past performance and best value (conformity to applicable and requested specifications). Past performance and specification conformity are significantly as important as price. Quotes shall be accepted up to 4 decimal places. Religious Certification Requirements for Meals Items offered on this bid must be certified Halal. Please read definitions below for requirement of each certification. Certified Halal items will be certified by a Halal Certification Agency, to meet the following requirements: With no pork or pork by-products; No traces of alcohol, or additives containing alcohol, including sugar alcohols; No gelatin derived from haram sources; No animal shortening derived from haram sources; No other mind-altering substances derived from haram sources; No forbidden enzymes derived from haram sources; No emulsifiers that are derived from haram sources; That has no exposure to haram foods or ingredients through cross contact. Quality assurance mechanisms to ensure no cross contact with haram food or ingredients. The animal from which the meat comes: Must be lawful to consume in Islamic Law. Cannot have died of cause other than proper slaughtering in accordance with Islam; The live animal must be slaughtered: By hand with an extremely sharp knife so that the animal suffers minimally; Intentionally slaughtered by a horizontal cut at the throat of the animal (below is laryngeal prominence), so that three of the four vessels are severed in one cut; By a practicing sane adult Muslim who is knowledgeable of the Islamic slaughtering procedures. The slaughterer must believe in all the essential matters of the Islamic faith. The slaughterer must recite Bismillah (In the Name of Allah) before the slaughter of each animal, and in a manner prescribed by Islamic law. The Halal slaughtered carcasses should be stamped and labeled as �Halal' Quoters will include a letter of certification from the religious certification agency dated no more than 11 months from the date of the quote provided. General Meal Specifications - Items 1 through 12 1) The tray for all meals will be: a) Made with non-metallic packaging that allows microwave and conventional oven heating and be heat sealed directly to the tray with clear plastic and wrapped with a separate sealed clear plastic wrapper which encloses the entire tray. b) A three-compartment tray with a large compartment of 21 fluid ounces and two compartments of 6 fluid ounces each. 2) All Meals will contain the food products per the individual product specification including the stated volume and/or weight of item as listed. 3) No substitutions may be made to the meats, vegetables, starches, sauces or preparation methods. 4) Meals (items 1 through 12) may be quoted as frozen and/or shelf stable products. Pricing must be identifiable as either frozen or shelf stable. 5) Each individual meal must be marked with the certification symbol from the religious certification agency. 6) Heating directions must be provided for various wattage microwaves or oven heating including recommended method. 7) Mixed Vegetables will contain carrots, corn, peas, green beans, and lima beans with: a) Not more than 40 percent by weight carrots. b) Not more than 40 percent by weight corn (sweet, golden or yellow, whole kernel com). c) Not more than 40 percent by weight green peas. 8) Peas and Carrots will contain: a) Not more than 40 percent by weight carrots. b) Not more than 40 percent by weight green peas. 9) Mashed Potatoes will be made with commercially prepared potato flakes without peel, adding only water according to the manufacturers� preparation instructions; or fresh potatoes prepared using only water and spices with only the amount of binder which will ensure the product does separate in processing. No extenders of any type are allowed. 10) Tomato Sauce will be commercially prepared or crushed and/or pureed tomatoes, tomato paste and spices using only the amount of binder required to ensure the product does not separate during processing. DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS/INSTRUCTIONS: Product(s) must meet Certified Menu Specifications; must have a legible expiration date that is at least 6 months past date delivered or will not be accepted All boxes/cases must be properly labeled (no write on labels or crossed out labels) All deliveries must be palletized unless prior arrangements were agreed to by warehouse staff. All non-frozen, perishable foods must be delivered between 34 degrees F and 40 degrees F. Any product that indicates prior thawing will be refused. All items must strictly follow the BOP Religious Diet Specifications. Food Service contractors have the responsibility of understanding these specifications. Contractors must obtain a copy of the Religious Diet Specifications prior to quoting. All items will be closely inspected. Some items may require thawing and cooking to determine specification compliance. Receipt of delivery may be conditional for a period of three (3) days to allow for adequate examination and testing. Items that fail to meet specifications will be refused. Items which are conditionally received and found noncompliant must be picked up at the vendors� expense within (2) weeks of noncompliance notification. If the product is not picked up within two (2) weeks, it will be disposed of by warehouse staff. Items that fail to meet specifications will be refused. All items must be dated. Deliveries will be accepted from 7:30 a.m. to 2:00 pm CST, Monday through Fridays, No deliveries on weekends or federal holidays. Delivery is on a first - come, first - serve basis. No delivery appointment is required. For any further delivery queries contact our Warehouse Supervisor at 817-782-4268. Unless otherwise stated within the specification of an item description in Section 2 of SF Form 1449, all dates for frozen food items must be delivered frozen and delivered before the best buy date, sell by date, use by date, best if used by date, or freeze by date on the label. Delivery vehicles should not exceed Gross 49000lbs-Tandem Axle 32000 Lbs. to comply with the bridge weight limit along the delivery route to the warehouse. Please mark all deliveries to reflect: Attn Food Service Department. Payments will be made upon complete delivery and acceptance of the product. Awards will be made via purchase order (EFT). title: N6449826R0524 - BOA Rotors
description: The Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD) intends to negotiate and award a sole source Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) to Argo Turboserve Corporation (ATC) as the only Authorized Distributor representing Curtiss Wright for OEM hardware components and support services for High Pressure (HP) and Low Pressure (LP) Propulsion Turbine Rotors and Propulsion Turbine and Ship Service Turbine Generator Overhaul Kits. Period of Performance: one base year plus two option years. DEFINITIONS/ACRONYMS A. Contract Discrepancy Report (CDR) : A report that the Government shall complete and issue to the Contractor when service is unsatisfactory and not in compliance with the terms and conditions of the contract. The Contractor is required to complete and return this form to the COR whenever performance is unsatisfactory. The CDR requires the Contractor to explain, in writing, the cause of the unsatisfactory performance, how performance will be returned to acceptable standards, and how reoccurrence of the problem will be prevented in the future. B. Contracting Officer (CO) : The individual with the authority to enter into, administer, and/or terminate contracts. The CO is the exclusive Government official authorized to execute changes and deviations or variations in the contract. C. Contracting Officer's Technical Representative (COTR) : A Government representative, designated in writing by the Contracting Officer, to be responsible for quality assurance, inspection, surveillance, documentation and acceptance of the Contractor's performance. A copy of the letter of designation will be provided to the Contractor. D. Preventive Maintenance (PM) : Services which are periodic in nature and are required to maintain the equipment in such condition that it may be operated in accordance with its intended design and functional capacity with minimal incidence of malfunction or inoperative conditions. To clean, lubricate, calibrate, test and replace faulty or worn parts and/or parts which are likely to become faulty, fail or become worn, repair or adjust components, or assemblies of components as necessitated by wear, tear, damage, or failure of parts, returning the equipment and/or instrument to the operating condition defined in the manufacturer s specifications. Friday to 12:00 P.M. Monday equals 24 hours). If days are indicated it shall mean calendar days including Saturdays, Sundays and Holidays. G.Rework. A documentation of services rendered for each incidence of work performance under the terms and conditions of the contract. I. Acronyms. Commonly used acronyms are listed below FSE: Field Service Engineer AQL: Acceptable Quality Level IAW: In Accordance With QA: Quality Assurance QC: Quality Control WS: Performance Work Statement VA: VA Medical Center CO: Contracting Officer COTR: Contracting Officer s Technical Representative FES: Facilities and Engineering Service PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE REQUIREMENTS Within 14 calendar days of Notice to Proceed, the vendor will submit to the COTR a written schedule of the planned PM visits for the coming year along with a written description of the work to be performed during each visit. Each inspection shall, at a minimum, include the following as specified for the equipment make, type, and time of seasonal operation. Any additional parts not identified in this document will not be covered by this contract. The vendor will obtain prior approval from the COTR prior to performing any additional repair work and the additional work will be billed separately. For each PM inspection, the contractor will provide a detailed written report to the COTR that summarizes work performed, problems/deficiencies found, and measurements taken. This report will be submitted within 10 calendar days of the date of PM inspection. All work will be performed between the hours of 7:30 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. on the prearranged dates. description: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Networking Contracting Office (NCO 01) located in Brockton, MA intends to enter into a sole source procurement, pursuant to the authority of FAR 6.302-1, with Airgas USA, LLC, for the following requirement: Statement of Work The Contractor shall provide Medical Grade Bulk Oxygen to the following Boston Veteran Affairs Medical Centers: Veterans Affairs Brockton 940 Belmont St Brockton, Ma. 02301-5596 Veterans Affairs Jamaica Plain 150 S. Huntington Ave. Jamaica Plain, Ma. 02130-4817 Veterans Affairs West Roxbury 1400 VFW Parkway West Roxbury, Ma. 02132-4927 Period of Performance: one base year plus one option year. General The purpose of this solicitation is to establish a committed source of supply of medical-grade liquid bulk oxygen for the three (3) locations within the VA BHS included in the solicitation. The Government facility does not own its own bulk oxygen tank(s), the contractor shall provide contractor-owned tanks with an appropriate back-up system (i.e. Reserve tank or cylinder bank). Specifications for each facility are listed in the solicitation schedule. The contract will be a Base year, and a six-month extension if needed utilizing the FAR 52.217-8 Option to Extend Services. Contracting Officer Representatives (COR) have been designated in the solicitation for the ordering facility. The CORs are responsible for local contract administration issues such as ordering and providing specific delivery instructions. Letters of delegation that outlines the COR s specific responsibilities will be provided to the contractor and COR at the time the contract award. The contractor will provide written procedures and training for VA staff for protocols to accomplish emergency shutdowns or other sudden, unplanned termination of the refilling process. Contractor will provide 24/7 emergency contact name(s) and telephone numbers (s). Contractor will provide annual alarm set-point testing and written verification must be presented through the use of a qualified third party expert per NFPA 99, 2002 Edition for contractor owned systems. Any code deficiencies as defined by NFPA55, Compressed Gases and Cryogenic Fluids code, must be identified by the contractor. A detailed explanation of these deficiencies must be presented in writing to the COR. Receipt of this written explanation must be signed for by the COR. Prior to first filling, the contractor must verify, in writing, the accuracy of all gauges on contractor owned tanks. 2.Acronyms 2.1 This section lists acronyms that are used in this Statement of Work and other parts of the solicitation. CCF 100 cubic feet CF Cubic feet CGA Compressed Gas Association CGMP Current Good Manufacturing Practices CO Contractor Owned COR Contracting Officer Representative DOT Department of Transportation FDA U.S. Food and Drug Administration GO Government Owned NFPA Nation Fire Protection Association OGA Other Government Agency (Other than VA) OSHA U.S. Department of Labor, Occupational Safety and Health Administration USP United States Pharmacopeia VA- Department of Veterans Affairs BHS Boston VA Healthcare System 3.Government Furnished Property 3.1 The solicitation schedule will identify the bulk oxygen tank(s) at each facility being Contractor Owned. Government owned property (alarm system) and appurtenances will be maintained by and at the expense of the government in a manner that will ensure compliance with applicable regulations, standards, and normal practices. 3.2 Each VA BHS location that requires installation of Contractor owned equipment shall provide a suitable location and foundation for the installation of the contractor owned bulk oxygen tank(s). Additionally, each facility shall provide access to an electrical power source and hook-up to a facility-maintained alarm system. The contractor shall perform the hook up of contractor owned equipment to the facility-maintained alarm system. 4. Contractor-Furnished Equipment 4.1 For those facilities listed in the schedule as having contractor owned tanks, the contractor shall provide, install, and maintain bulk oxygen tank (s) with appropriate back-up system(s) and telemetry monitoring of all systems. Through the duration of the contract, the contractor shall be liable for the integrity, suitability, and safety of contractor owned tank(s) that shall ensure compliance with applicable regulations, standards, and normal good practices. The tank capacity and reserve system shown in the schedule are minimum capacities required by the using facilities. Manifold, cylinders for the reserve supply, liquid converter, alarm switch, regulator, valves level indicator, and any other devices or connections required for proper tie-ins with the facility s gas system shall be furnished by the contractor, without cost to the Government. The manifold or liquid converter shall deliver gas at a pressure and rate of flow adequate to supply the system. Each Liquid oxygen storage container shall have an outlet that allows access for testing the purity of the oxygen. 4.2 All equipment and materials required to perform on the contract (other than what is specifically listed in section 3, Government-Furnished Property) shall be provided by the contractor. Contractor owned equipment shall be installed, inspected, and maintained by the contractor without additional cost to the Government. (i.e. all installation, inspection and maintenance costs shall be included in the contract s monthly equipment rental fee for the applicable facility.) Contractor owned equipment shall be kept in good operating condition and appearance, in accordance with applicable regulations, standards and normal good practices. The contractor shall be provided reasonable access to the bulk oxygen systems for this purpose. 5. If the contractor s equipment replaces equipment already in use, the exchange of equipment shall be accomplished without interruption of gas supply to the using facility. Contractor installed equipment shall remain the property of the contractor and shall be removed upon termination of the contract, when directed by the ordering facility and in full cooperation with the succeeding contractor to avoid interruption of gas supply. 5.2 All contractor owned equipment shall be installed in accordance with NFPA 55 compressed Gases and Cryogenic Fluids Code: 2010, and FDA s Current Good Manufacturing Practices (CGMP) Regulations. The contractor shall comply with all OSHA standards and applicable safety requirements, including proper signage and use of personal protective equipment. 6. Delivery of Medical Liquid Bulk Oxygen 6.1 Bulk oxygen is ordered by and delivered to the individual ordering facilities. The list of facilities and information regarding their unique delivery requirements is included in the solicitation schedule. 6.2 The contractor shall deliver medical-grade liquid oxygen within the timeframe specified in the schedule for each VA BHS location. The timeframe identified may be either the number of calendar days after receipt of the Government s order, the specific days of the week for delivery, the specific time intervals between deliveries, a specified reorder point, or other specified ordering and delivery methods.
