title: BATDOK Family of Systems (FoS)
description: Please review the full RFI document (Atch 1) for full details and instructions. A. Notice to Respondents This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for information and planning purposes in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.201(e). It is not a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or Commercial Solutions Opening, and it is not a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not pay for information submitted or for any cost incurred in responding. Responses will not be returned, and the Government will not provide feedback or evaluations to individual respondents. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. Respondents are responsible for appropriately marking proprietary information. The Government will protect properly marked information from disclosure and may share responses with Government support contractors bound by non-disclosure agreements. Do not submit classified information. B. Purpose The Defense Health Agency (DHA), Program Acquisition Executive, Medical Digital Solutions (PAE MDS), Joint Operational Medicine Information Systems (JOMIS) Program Management Office (PMO), is issuing this RFI to conduct market research for the operations and sustainment (O&S) of the Battlefield Assisted Trauma Distributed Observation Kit (BATDOK) family of systems (FoS). The anticipated period of performance begins 1 October 2027 (Fiscal Year 2028). The BATDOK FoS is comprised of BATDOK-J, an Android and iOS mobile application for point-of-injury (PoI) casualty documentation; BATDOK Link, a Windows operating system application plug-in that allows for the transfer of data from BATDOK-J into MHS GENESIS Theater (MHSG-T) or Operational Medicine Data Service (OMDS) via QR code; and BAT-TAK, a plug-in for the Android Team Awareness Kit (ATAK). The FoS is a mature capability, fielded and in operational use across the Military Services. The purpose of this RFI is to: Identify potential sources, including small businesses, with demonstrated DoW experience developing, sustaining, and integrating tactical mobile applications on the Android and iOS operating systems, together with associated ATAK and Windows plug-ins; Obtain industry input on technical approaches, best practices, and innovations for achieving the outcomes described in the Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) in Part II; and Inform the Government�s acquisition strategy, including contract vehicle, contract type, small business set-aside determination, and refinement of the requirement and its performance measures.

description: *** Please be advised that this RFI - Market Research is posted under both NAICS codes 483113 and 483111 to ensure the broadest possible industry dissemination. The postings are identical; interested parties need submit only one response. *** November 3, 2026 Attention Maritime Transportation / Ocean Freight industry partners: Request for Information (RFI) � Market Research for Ocean Transportation of Hazardous Waste (Guam to CONUS) The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is conducting a market survey to determine the commercial availability and operational capacity of ocean carriers to transport government-generated hazardous waste from the Territory of Guam to permitted facilities in the United States. Pursuant to the Military Cargo Preference Act (10 U.S.C. � 2631) and coastwise trade statutes under 46 U.S.C. Chapter 551, the Government is evaluating the availability of qualified U.S.-flagged vessels, including coastwise-endorsed vessels and U.S.-flagged vessels operating under registry endorsements in accordance with the statutory Guam trade exemption (46 U.S.C. � 12111(b)). This market survey assesses industry capability to meet technical environmental safety standards and required volume throughput, while establishing factual market data regarding whether domestic vessel capacity is sufficient or if alternative statutory authorities, such as the hazardous waste transport exception under 46 U.S.C. � 55105(b) or applicable administrative waiver procedures must be evaluated to ensure mission readiness and regulatory compliance. 1. The current Cargo Description and Operational Requirements for DLA are: a. Cargo Type: Department of War (DoW) Generated Hazardous Waste. The waste streams include a broad range of materials, including: i. RCRA-regulated hazardous waste: Waste exhibiting ignitability (D001), corrosivity (D002), reactivity (D003), or toxicity characteristics, including waste containing lead, chromium, cadmium, mercury, benzene, and other hazardous constituents. ii. Contaminated liquids: Waste fuels, gasoline, solvents, paints, thinners, corrosive liquids, contaminated wastewater, and other petroleum- or chemically contaminated liquids. iii. Used oil and petroleum-related waste: Used lubricating oil, oily water, oil filters, sludge, and petroleum contaminated materials, some of which may be managed as non-RCRA-regulated waste. iv. Batteries: Lithium-ion batteries, lithium-metal batteries, lead-acid batteries, nickel-cadmium batteries, and other spent batteries requiring regulated transportation or disposal. v. Contaminated solids: Paint debris, spent blasting media, contaminated soil, oily rags, absorbents, filters, and other solids contaminated with hazardous substances. vi. Other hazardous materials and waste: Oxidizers, corrosive chemicals, flammable substances, aerosol waste, and compressed gas cylinders, where applicable. The cargo includes both RCRA hazardous waste requiring a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest and other regulated or non-hazardous waste streams. Individual shipments vary in composition and may contain materials classified under multiple DOT/IMDG hazard classes, including Classes 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, and 9. b. Waste is generally packaged in approved drums, intermediate bulk containers (IBCs), or other appropriate containers and consolidated into 40-foot shipping containers. Bulk liquid waste may also be transported in ISO tank containers. The applicable waste classifications, quantities, and packaging are identified on the corresponding waste profiles, manifests, and shipping documents. c. Hazard Class/UN Number Required: (See Attached List.) d. Required Weekly Throughput Estimate: 2 Each � (40-Foot Container�s) e. Route: Guam to United States (West Coast) f. Required Shipping Window: Present � Indefinite Interested industry partners are requested to submit a written response to this Request for Information (RFI) within twenty (20) calendar days from the date of publication of this notice. This will enable the Government to thoroughly evaluate commercial market capacity, operational feasibility, and statutory compliance. Submissions should directly address the following required questions: 1. Company Information a. Company Legal Name: b. Company Cage Code: c. Physical Address: d. Website: e. Primary NAICS code: f. Business Size (large / small): g. Any socioeconomic status, if any: 2. Point of Contact a. Name: b. Title: c. Phone: d. Email: 3. Status: Does your company currently operate a Jones Act-compliant vessel scheduled on this route during the specified shipping window? 4. Technical Certification: Is your company legally certified and operationally equipped to accept, stow, and transport all the specific classes of hazardous waste listed? (See attached �DLA-GUAM � Hazardous Waste List�.) 5. Volume and Throughput Capacity? (Critical): 6. What is the maximum volume (measured in standard Conex/ISO container equivalents) that your company can commit to transporting on this route per week for the DoW, and DoW Contractors for the Hazard Class/UN Number Required? 7. Can your company meet or exceed the military's minimum required throughput of 2 Each � 40-Foot Container�s (or equivalent) without causing operational or regulatory storage backlogs in Guam? 8. If your company can only offer partial or restricted capacity (e.g., limiting transport to 1 container per week/voyage), please provide specific operational, regulatory, or safety constraints dictating this volume limit. Commercial Intent: If your company possesses both the technical capability and the required volume capacity, is your company willing to support the DoW, and DoW Contractors executing the removal of hazardous waste from Guam? Justification for Refusal: If your company is unable or unwilling to accept this cargo, or cannot meet the required weekly volume throughput, please state the specific technical, regulatory, safety, or vessel allocation reasons for your refusal/capacity limitation. This RFI-Market Research does not constitute a solicitation and does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation, award a contract, or pay for information submitted in response to this notice. The Government will utilize the provided data, as well as any omissions, to assess commercial capability, capacity, availability, procurement strategies, and hazardous waste transportation exceptions. Please submit your written response directly to Bradley Moehlig at Bradley.Moehlig@dla.mil & Mike Mamaty at Michael.Mamaty@dla.mil . Submissions should be delivered electronically via email in Adobe PDF or Microsoft Word format. Please referencing Subject Line: 'Response to RFI � Maritime Transport of Hazardous Waste (Guam to CONUS)'. Timely submission of capabilities, vessel availability, and commercial operating constraints will directly inform DLA's acquisition strategy, small business determinations, and required statutory compliance determinations under federal maritime law.

title: FMC Carswell 2 QTR FY27 National Menu Solicitation
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul FAR Subpart 12.2, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The solicitation number is 15B50527Q00000008 and is issued as a Request for Quote (RFQ). This Solicitation is for 2nd Qtr FY27 National Menu Solicitation. The solicitation document, incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Revolutionary FAR Overhaul issuance date May 2, 2025. This solicitation is issued as Total small business set-aside. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 311999 with a small business size standard of 700.00 employees. FOB Destination shall be to: FMC Carswell Food Service Department 1200 Meandering Road, Fort Worth, Texas 76114. Items will be awarded individually. More than one item may be awarded to one offeror/contractor. Award will be given to the offeror whose bid/quote conforms to the requirements and is determined to provide the best value to the Government. The following are the evaluation factors that will be used to evaluate each offeror are price, past performance and conformity to applicable and requested specifications. Past performance and specification conformity are significantly as important as price. Quotes shall be accepted up to 4 decimal places. DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS/INSTRUCTIONS: Product(s) must meet Certified Menu Specifications; must have a legible expiration date that is at least 6 months past date delivered or will not be accepted No dented cans All boxes/cases must be properly labeled (no write on labels or crossed out labels) All deliveries must be palletized unless prior arrangements were agreed to by warehouse staff. All non-frozen, perishable foods must be delivered between 34 degrees F and 40 degrees F. All canned goods must be delivered above 34 degrees F and not frozen. Any product that indicates prior thawing will be refused. All items must strictly follow the BOP Religious Diet Specifications. Food Service contractors have the responsibility of understanding these specifications. Contractors must obtain a copy of the Religious Diet Specifications prior to quoting. All items will be closely inspected. Some items may require thawing and cooking to determine specification compliance. Receipt of delivery may be conditional for a period of three (3) days to allow for adequate examination and testing. Items that fail to meet specifications will be refused. Items which are conditionally received and found noncompliant must be picked up at the vendors� expense within (2) weeks of noncompliance notification. If the product is not picked up within two (2) weeks, it will be disposed of by warehouse staff. Items that fail to meet specifications will be refused. All items must be dated. Deliveries will be accepted from 7:30 a.m. to 2:00 pm CST, Monday through Fridays, No deliveries on weekends or federal holidays. Delivery is on a first - come, first - serve basis. No delivery appointment is required. For any further delivery queries contact our Warehouse Supervisor at 817-782-4268. Unless otherwise stated within the specification of an item description in Section 2 of SF Form 1449, all dates for frozen food items must be delivered frozen and delivered before the best buy date, sell by date, use by date, best if used by date, or freeze by date on the label. Delivery vehicles should not exceed Gross 49000lbs-Tandem Axle 32000 Lbs. to comply with the bridge weight limit along the delivery route to the warehouse. Please mark all deliveries to reflect: Attn Food Service Department. Payments will be made upon complete delivery and acceptance of the product. Awards will be made via purchase order (EFT). Invoices are to be sent electronically to CRW-BusinessOffice-S@bop.gov. Requested delivery period is January 4 - January 29, 2026. Please read the attached solicitation document in entirety, noting the requested information, specifications, types and packaging sizes as applicable. Quotes Submission Instructions: Contractor/Offeror MUST be registered and ACTIVE on sam.gov when responding to this solicitation and throughout this contract opportunity. This is a requirement to conduct business with the federal government. Failure to have an active entity might lead to your solicitation response not being considered. This solicitation is a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside. Offerors are solely responsible for ensuring that their small business representations and certifications are current and accurately reflected within their SAM.gov entity profile. All quotes and bids pertaining to this solicitation must be received by the designated point of contact no later than November 25, 2026, at 12:00 PM Central Time (CT). All quotes and bids will be received via email ONLY to ekarua@bop.gov. Use the attached solicitation document when submitting your quotes. No other form of quotes will be accepted. All quotes or questions will be received electronically to the primary contact listed below (ekarua@bop.gov) Kindly complete section 17(a) Contractor/ Vendor information as well as section 30 (a & b). Availability of Funds (FAR 52.232-18): Funds are not presently available for this acquisition past Dec 11, 2026. The Government's obligation under this solicitation is contingent upon the availability of appropriate funds from which payment for contract purposes can be made. No legal liability on the part of the Government for any payment may arise until funds are made available to the Contracting Officer for this contract and until the Contractor receives notice of such availability, to be confirmed in writing by the Contracting Officer. title: Rustici Content Controller License Renewal
description: Air Force Installation Contracting Center (AFICC) 338 ESS, JBSA-Randolph, TX is conducting an acquisition for Rustici Content Controller License Renewal. Rustici Content Controller represents a critical component of AETC's Digital Learning Services Architecture (DLSA) myLearning system. It is a central dynamic content hub to scale distribution to LMSs across multiple eLearning standards while maintaining visibility into learner engagement. It imports and tests course packages, sets up licenses to control who can access the content, shares courses out to any LMS via proxy dispatch packages, and tracks the results with built-in aggregate reporting and analytics to guarantee maximum system availability and mission readiness. The contractor shall deliver authentic, manufacturer-authorized Rustici Content Controller software licenses, support, maintenance, and new releases for the DLSA-myLearning system serving up to 800,000 users. The commercial COTS product must support enterprise administration, customized branding, reporting, standard content import/export, and seamless integration with government-approved host environments. To ensure platform integrity on the DoDIN, all software components must strictly comply with AFI 17-130 (Air Force Cybersecurity Program Management), meet the evaluation and validation mandates of DoDI 8500.01 and CNSSP-11, and utilize cryptographic modules conforming to FIPS 140-3 standards. title: Lunar Node - 2 Radio System
description: NASA/MSFC has a requirement for the development and delivery of hardware and firmware for the Lunar Node - 2 payload to support a rapid path to integration and flight payload development. Key considerations of this action are focused on the ability to deliver a flight-ready payload within 90 days, which requires maintaining physical, electrical, and software interfaces to the existing design. NASA/MSFC intends to issue a sole source contract to acquire the following items and services from Amergint Technologies Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of CACI, Inc.-Federal under the authority of FAR 6.103-1, 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." Amergint is uniquely qualified to complete this work as the designer, developer, implementer, and owner of the SWIFT-SLX platform. Selection of Amergint utilizes their existing hardware and proprietary technology (including its structure, electronics, interfaces, and antenna) for this mission to meet the project's accelerated deadline while also upgrading capability without requiring interface changes that would impact schedule. The procurement includes multiple potential tasks/items as necessary to prepare the payload for a future flight opportunity: (1) A study to provide insight and detailed schedule for development time for addition of two-way coherent ranging into the flight platform. Analyze and assess feasibility for potential paths for upgrades and improvements to the existing SWIFT SLX-X EDU that the Lunar Node - 1 project has on-hand to support potential lunar operations as part of Lunar Node - 2. Utilize existing hardware from the Lunar Node - 1 payload, including its structure, electronics, interfaces, and antenna. To meet the desired deadline while also adding upgraded capability of high value to the program, the payload cannot accommodate any interface changes. This includes onboard firmware, software, electrical, and mechanical interfaces. (2) Re-work on the existing SWIFT-SLX previously delivered to MSFC. This includes disassembly, conformal coating and staking of internal electronics, reassembly and functional checkouts. (3) A current build of the SWIFT-SLX for an Engineering Development Unit (EDU) and flight platform. (4) A new EDU to match current capabilities and flight design. (5) Upgraded firmware to enable additional capability on the LN-1 SWIFT-SLX radio to enable two-way coherent ranging on the platform using S-band frequencies. The Government intends to acquire a commercial product or service using FAR Part 12. Interested organizations may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort electronically via email to Cynthia Hubbard at cynthia.a.hubbard@nasa.gov and Brent Evans at brent.l.evans@nasa.gov not later than 12:00 P.M. C.D.T. on November 25, 2026. Such capabilities/qualifications will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct this acquisition on a competitive basis. A decision by the Government not to compete this acquisition on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition can be found at: https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/regs/Procurement-Ombuds- Comp-Advocate-Listing.pdf

description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION a. The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), Naval Test Wing Atlantic (NTWL), Air Test and Evaluation Squadron TWO ONE (HX-21), Patuxent River, MD, has a follow-on requirement for Contractor Maintenance Support (CMS) Services to perform Organizational Level (O-Level) maintenance support services on assigned CH-53K test aircraft. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Sources Sought will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set[1]Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this Sources Sought is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the Request for Proposal (RFP). This is for the NAWCAD HX-21 CH-53K O-LEVEL CMS. This is a follow-on requirement. The current contract information can be found in Section 3.0, paragraph b below. There have been significant changes to the scope as follows: estimated on-site personnel increasing from 62 FTEs to 75 FTEs. This is not subject to bundling or consolidation. b. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE AND CONTRACT/PROGRAM BACKGROUND a. Anticipated Contract Type: C-Type Contract with Firm Fixed Price (FFP) CLINs for Labor and Cost Reimbursable CLINs for associated Other Direct Costs (ODCs). The Government is anticipating an additional Cost Reimbursable Performance Incentive CLIN. The anticipated Period of Performance includes one base period of 12 months with four one[1]year option periods for a total potential performance period of 5 years. b. The incumbent contract information is as follows: Incumbent Contractor: Adams Communication & Engineering Technology, Inc. Contract Number: N68520-20-D-0032 / N00421-23-F-0619 Contract End Date: 13 Aug 2028 Contract Type: FFP Previous Set-Aside Designation: Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) Number of FTEs on the Contract: 62 FTEs c. Program Background: HX-21 has a follow-on requirement for CMS Services to perform O-Level (to include limited Intermediate Level (I-Level) and Depot Level (D[1]Level)) maintenance support services and other explicit test support tasks required to maintain assigned CH-53K aircraft to the proper standards required to meet the requirements of the HX-21 test schedule. The limited I-Level and D-Level work is contingent, provided skilled artisans and required tools are available and authorization is received from the cognizant authority. Services include aircraft maintenance and logistics support on aircraft, aircraft systems, and Support Equipment (SE) for which HX-21 has cognizant responsibility. The majority of work performance will be accomplished at Patuxent River, Maryland. description: The US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Walla Walla District is seeking business sources for a supply contract entitled: Little Goose & Lower Granite Dams Wicket Gate Locks. The work involves precision fabrication, testing, and delivery to Little Goose Lock and Dam and Lower Granite Lock and Dam located in Washington State. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this project is 332710 (Machine Shops), associated with Product Service Code (PSC) 2830 (Water Turbines and Water Wheels; and Components). The associated small business size standard is 500 employees. ATTACHMENT NOTICE: Draft Statement of Work (SOW) and draft technical drawings are attached to this notice for industry review. Responding firms should reference these documents when answering the questions within this sources sought notice. Is your company able to submit an ISO 9001:2015, AS9100, or equivalent Quality Management System (QMS) certification at time of solicitation? What is the anticipated lead time for delivery of described fabricated items based on the attached draft documents? Are there any market conditions or industry practices that you feel the Government needs to be aware of? Summary of Scope of Work The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers requires the precision fabrication, testing, and delivery of new Wicket Gate Locks for the Little Goose and Lower Granite hydroelectric dams. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform the manufacturing and delivery of these critical load-bearing infrastructure components. Fabrication & Machining (See Attached Draft SOW & Drawings) Precision machining and manufacturing of steel structural components in strict accordance with the attached draft drawings and SOW. Quality Control & Testing Standards Higher-Level Quality: The manufacturing facility must adhere to Higher-Level Contract Quality standards (ISO 9001:2015, AS9100, or equivalent QMS) to ensure strict geometric tolerances and material integrity are met. Welding & NDT: Welding operators, welders, and tack welders, must be qaulified in accordance with Section 4, Part C or AWS D1.1/D1.1M. title: Trenching, Conduit and Ground-well Installation
description: Description The United Stated Embassy in Kingston is requesting proposals for Trenching, Conduit And Ground-Well Installation in various locations on the Embassy compound. The contractor will provide all labor, equipment, supervision, material specific to the back filling and compaction and management needed to complete the job Infrastructure Support System - Handhole / Underground Conduit System Trenching Nine locations have been identified requiring trench work. Thirteen locations have been identified requiring trench work. Before excavation, the Contractor shall locate and verify all existing utilities in the proposed trench alignment. If excavation interferes with existing drains, piping, or structures, the Contractor shall immediately notify, in writing, the COR and provide temporary protection for these systems before proceeding. Trenching from Handholes The Contractor shall make wall penetrations into existing manholes/handholes as required for the number and size of conduits entering and exiting each structure, in accordance with the drawings. Conduit Existing conduit shall remain in place unless the drawings specifically direct removal or modification. Under grass, soil, the Contractor shall install Schedule 80 PVC conduit with a minimum cover of 24 inches (610 mm) from finished grade to top of conduit, or as indicated on the drawings, whichever is greater. All underground 90 degree bends with a 12inch (305 mm) radius shall use prefabricated sweeping bends. Above grade, all underground PVC conduit shall transition to rigid galvanized steel (RGS) using PVC to RGS couplers. The Contractor shall install pull lines in all new conduit runs. Soil and Backfill Materials Soil Materials The Contractor shall provide all labor and materials for soil and backfill, where required. Select Backfill: ASTM D 2487 soil classification groups SW, SP, and SM, or combinations thereof; free of rock or gravel larger than 3 inches (75 mm), debris, waste, frozen materials, vegetation, and other deleterious matter. Asphalt/Concrete Base Course: Naturally or artificially graded mixture of natural or crushed gravel, crushed stone, and natural or crushed sand; ASTM D 2940; with at least 95% passing a 11/2inch (40 mm) sieve and not more than 8% passing a 1/4inch (6.4 mm) sieve. Base Gravel: Naturally or artificially graded mixture of natural or crushed gravel, crushed stone, and natural or crushed sand; ASTM D 2940; 100% passing a 1inch (25 mm) sieve and not more than 8% passing a 1/4inch (6.4 mm) sieve. Sand Cushion: ASTM C 33 fine aggregate, natural or manufactured sand. Placement and Compaction Place backfill and fill in layers not exceeding: 8 inches (203 mm) loose thickness for heavy compaction equipment; 4 inches (102 mm) loose thickness when compacted by hand-operated tampers. Place backfill and fill evenly to the required elevations, uniformly along their full length. Compact soil materials to not less than the following percentages of maximum dry unit weight per ASTM D 1557: Under lawns or unpaved areas: scarify and re-compact top 6 inches (152 mm) below subgrade and compact each layer to 85%. Utility trenches: compact each layer of initial and final backfill to 85%. Anticipated Period of Performance: a base period of twenty-one (21) days after contract award Eligibility and Registration Offerors must hold an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) when they submit a proposal and at award. You are to provide the full names of the attendees, the vehicle information to include make, model, color and plate number of the vehicle being driven. The email must be sent no later than Wednesday, November 04, 2026 by 2 pm. Completed proposal are to be email to kingstonquotes@state.gov in PDF format by the deadline stipulated.

Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. title: Chesapeake and Delaware (C and D) Canal Building Replacement Project.
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineer (USACE), Philadelphia District (NAP), anticipates a requirement for the Chesapeake and Delaware (C and D) Canal Building Replacement Project. The Chesapeake and Delaware or Canal connects the Delaware River to the Chesapeake Bay and Port of Baltimore. The canal is maintained from a field office located in Chesapeake City Maryland. This office consists of multiple buildings and shops that are essential to the continued operation of the canal. Several of these building have reached the end of their lifecycle and need to be replaced. This project will include the demolition and consolidation of the mechanics shop, bridge shop and storage buildings. A new building will be constructed to sever as a replacement of the buildings that are being removed. The building will be located along the east side of the project site. The building dimensions will be 60 feet x 150 feet with a clear ceiling height of 20 feet. The building will have a gable roof with the ridge running parallel to the length of the building. A pre- engineered metal building with tapered columns will be used. The columns will be enclosed with steel stud framing and gypsum board in the office areas. Vehicle and workshop areas will have propane fired heating. Office areas will be provided with air conditioning. The electrical service will be upgraded if necessary to provide power to the new building. The building will be connected into backup power from the existing diesel generator. Work will consist of the following activities: A.) The project scope includes all work required to design and construct a 9,000 square foot maintenance building in accordance with the Request for Proposal documents including the demolition of the four existing buildings and propane storage tank currently located at the site. Utilities serving each of the buildings being demolished must be demolished to the extents defined in section 02 41 00 Demolition. Requirements stated in this contract are minimums. Innovative, creative, and life cycle cost effective solutions, which meet or exceed these requirements are encouraged. Further, the Offeror is encouraged to seek solutions that will expedite construction (panelization, pre-engineered, etc.) and shorten the schedule. The intent of the Government is to emphasize the placement of funds into functional/operational requirements. Materials and methods must reflect this by choosing the most economical type of construction allowed by code for this occupancy/project. B.) The maintenance building must be provided with Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC), electrical, communications, fire protection, life safety, plumbing systems, waste oil storage, and compressed air systems. C.) A 3,000 square foot storage shed must be designed and constructed at the location identified on the site plan. The shed design must include power and lighting. D.) The scope of work also includes civil site work consisting of site paving, installation of stormwater drainage, connection into the domestic water utility, sanitary sewer utility connection for the new maintenance building, connection of existing sanitary sewer lines into the towns sanitary sewer utility, a vehicle wash area and fire hydrants. Site work is shown in Appendix A. Site electrical work must be completed to provide the maintenance building and storage shed with power fed from the existing switch gear shed. Site telecommunications work must be completed to provide the maintenance building with connection into the existing telecommunications utilities. E.) A propane storage tank must be provided onsite and be connected to the new maintenance building and the existing propane fired generator. The estimated period of performance will be 730 calendar days. The estimated magnitude of this project is between $5,000,000 and $15,000,000. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, with an SBA Size standard of $45.0M.

title: FY27 42LRS Local Drayage Services
description: The 42nd Logistics Readiness Squadron has identified the critical need for a Packing and Crating Contract to manage the relocation and deployment of household goods and mission-essential items for Airmen and their families. This service is essential for maintaining operational readiness, as it ensures that Airman have timely access to both personal belongings and equipment needed to complete their mission. Without this support, Airmen may face delays in receiving essential items, impacting their ability to perform their duties effectively and compromising mission success. The absence of household goods can affect the morale and well-being of Airmen and their families, potentially leading to stress that distracts from their focus on the mission. Meeting this logistical need is therefore vital for mission readiness and for supporting the well-being of Airmen, enabling them to remain fully engaged and effective in the roles. Please be aware that this is just a Request for Information and no contract will result from this posting.

The anticipated disciplines include Surveying. Building measurement and verification of existing utilities are expressly supported by the SOW. It requires a thorough as-built investigation and independent field verification of dimensions, wall layouts, utilities, material types, and other design conditions. The notice does not expressly require a boundary survey, campus-wide utility survey, or site topographic survey. It also does not define survey limits, accuracy, deliverables, or whether licensed land-surveying services are intended. Therefore: Existing-building measured documentation: required. Verification of utilities affecting the design: required. Can the VA clarify whether replacement of the air handling unit(s) serving the renovated 2nd Floor area is anticipated as part of this project, or whether the design should evaluate and determine HVAC system modifications necessary to support the renovated space? VA architectural guidance likewise calls for investigating whether existing systems have sufficient capacity for renovations. That guidance does not establish that these particular AHUs require replacement Will the 2nd Floor space be vacated during construction or will phased construction be required? title: Veterans Affairs St. Louis Health Care System (VASTLHCS) John Cochran (JC) Hospital in St. Louis, Missouri
description: ****Amend 0006 posted 20261023: Provide additional updates based on bidder inquiries****Amend 0005 posted 20261021: Provide additional updates based on bidder inquiries****Amend 0004 posted 20261002: Provide additional updates based on bidder inquiries****Amend 0003 posted 20260925: Provide updates based on bidder inquiries****Amend 0002 posted 20260902: Provide specifics for the site visit****Amend 0001 posted 20260817: Provide correct Plans Room Key****VA Hospital Solicitation Notice W912DQ26RA060. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Kansas City District is issuing a solicitation for an Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) services delivery method contract for the construction of a new bed tower, clinical expansion, parking garage in support of the Veterans Affairs St. Louis Health Care System (VASTLHCS) John Cochran (JC) Hospital in St. Louis, Missouri. Offerors shall submit an offer subject to Project Labor Agreement (PLA) requirements in accordance with RFO 22.5, Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects. Any PLA reached pursuant to the PLA requirements in the solicitation does not change the terms of the contract or provide for any price adjustment by the Government. Funds are fully available for this requirement. The project will be solicited as full and open (unrestricted). The requirements under this construction project include right sizing the VAs medical center by demolishing several deficient and underutilized buildings and then constructing multiple new modern and seismically compliant structures and facilities on the same, expanded site. The newly constructed facilities are incorporated into a master plan for future expansion and demolition of additional primary facilities. The new primary facilities will be acquired using the Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) delivery method which includes a Pre-Construction Services Phase. The Government will evaluate the performance capability of offerors in accordance with the criteria described in the solicitation resulting in a single award under the best value continuum using the trade-off process in accordance with RFO 15.103-1 to the responsible offeror whose proposal the source selection authority determines conforms to the solicitation, is fair and reasonable, and offers the best overall value to the government, considering non-priced factors described in the solicitation and price. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236220, (Commercial and Institutional Building Construction), with a small business size standard of $45 million in average annual receipts. The estimated construction magnitude is over $1,000,000,000. The estimated performance period for the pre-construction services phase is 820 calendar days from Notice to Proceed (NTP).Interested offerors must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM). If the offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity must have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. A Proposal Guarantee will be required with your proposal in the amount of 20% of the Offerors proposed price or $3,000,000, whichever is less. Payment and Performance Bonds will be required for the full amount (100%) of the awarded contract before the Notice to Proceed can be issued. Point of Contact: The point of contact for all questions/inquiries is Michael France at michael.g.france@usace.army.mil and David Walsh (Contracting Officer) at david.j.walsh@usace.army.mil.

title: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Marshalling Services - Yuma, AZ
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Marshalling Services 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required on or about January 1, 2027 � December 31, 2030 in Yuma, AZ. Interested parties must be located within 50 miles of the Yuma, AZ area. The vendor must be the owner or legal lessee of the facility. Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. Encourage maximum participation by offering a range of non-government affiliated services (retail financing, aftermarket warranties, vehicle enhancement etc.). Store, service and remarket of electric vehicles to include any necessary charging infrastructure. Transport vehicles to and from vendor locations. Prepare vehicles for public inspection and final sales/disposition, including services such as reconditioning, maintenance and repair, as well as equipment removal/disposal, and license plate & government credit card disposal and tracking. Offer industry-aligned services for customers to perform vehicle test drives. Provide state-of-the-art technology that will improve customer experience including enhanced condition reporting, 360� views, video, high-definition photography, etc. Conduct a full and open competitive sales process, including public inspection periods for all vehicles, and any related sale services for exchange/sale property. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage, and release of vehicles from time of receipt until final removal. Manage the logistics of vehicle transportation to bring vehicles to sale. Prepare vehicles for sale, to include vehicle equipment removal/disposal, reconditioning, and repairs. Work with local government entities to facilitate any inspections, documentation, and any other actions required to complete transactions in local markets. Perform electronic inventory management, vehicle inspection, complete condition reporting for vehicles. Offer recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, local market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Provide customer service to buyers in global markets. Create and execute marketing campaigns for local markets. Offer an internet sales platform with the potential to reach a global audience. Collect proceeds from vehicle sales and if necessary, convert to U.S. dollars. Marshalling only site tasks include, but are not limited to: Transport or resource/transportation of vehicles to and from vendor location (e.g., customer location, OEM dealership, offsite repair facility). Inspect vehicles upon delivery for various factors including but not limited to any damage to the vehicle, all components of the vehicle are accounted for (e.g., keys, floor mats, etc.), and missing equipment. Perform telematics device installation and/or activation on all new vehicles prior to releasing the vehicle to the customer. Validate new vehicles and options to vehicle order information provided by GSA. Perform pre-delivery inspections (PDI) in accordance with the manufacturer�s standards. Prepare new vehicles for customer receipt. Provide driver education for customers including vehicle operation, unique features, infotainment settings, etc. Offer specialized expertise and support on Electric Vehicle management, operation and charging infrastructure. Charge battery-powered vehicles. Maintain all vehicle fuel and charge levels as prescribed in the Statement of Work by GSA. Perform custodial and sales preparation services to facilitate auction house sales of GSA exchange lease vehicles. Process and manage all required vehicle shipment and delivery documentation. Manage scheduled vehicle appointments and ensure accurate vehicle exchanges. Perform all necessary tasks associated with confirming vehicle assignment and termination to and from the customer as prescribed by GSA. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to GSA Fleet and customer agencies throughout the marshalling process to ensure a seamless and transparent delivery and exchange process. Fulfill proper disposal of old/expired plates both front and back as prescribed by GSA. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage and inventory control of vehicles, license plates, credit cards and other assets from time of receipt until final removal. Scale charging capabilities to meet the needs of increasing electric vehicle adoption. 2.0 Background GSA Fleet provides a full-service fleet management program providing transportation solutions to partner agencies worldwide across the U.S. Federal government. It maintains a diverse fleet of over 250,000 vehicles, including light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, to include sedans, SUVs, vans, trucks, buses, ambulances, and law enforcement vehicles. Vehicles range from gasoline and diesel fueled vehicles to alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs), such as electric vehicles (EVs) to low-speed electric vehicles (LSEV�s) and non-powered vehicles and trailers. Nationally, GSA Fleet orders and receives on average 30,000+ vehicles from suppliers annually. As GSA Fleet is responsible for the disposition of its vehicles, it then remarkets and sells the used vehicles across the United States and its territories, Japan, and Europe. Its vehicles are sold under the exchange/sale authority of 41 CFR 102-39. This authority aims to expedite the disposal process and maximize proceeds in the most cost-effective manner to the U.S. taxpayer. To achieve this objective, GSA Fleet currently sells its used vehicles via live and online auctions worldwide, leveraging its contracts with commercial vendors to carry out all auction-related services. These auctions must adhere to all legal and regulatory requirements. They must also be open to the general public and provide an equal opportunity for individuals, businesses, government entities, and other organizations to take part in a zero-fee, fully open, and competitive sales process. To facilitate this process, GSA Fleet employs its vehicle remarketing specialists, who are warranted sales contracting officers and experts in the sales of its vehicles, to work with its vendors to approve repairs, pricing, as well as carry out and approve each sale to maximize net proceeds. description: ****Amend 0005 posted 20261021: Provide additional updates based on bidder inquiries****Amend 0004 posted 20261002: Provide additional updates based on bidder inquiries****Amend 0003 posted 20260925: Provide updates based on bidder inquiries****Amend 0002 posted 20260902: Provide specifics for the site visit****Amend 0001 posted 20260817: Provide correct Plans Room Key****VA Hospital Solicitation Notice W912DQ26RA060. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Kansas City District is issuing a solicitation for an Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) services delivery method contract for the construction of a new bed tower, clinical expansion, parking garage in support of the Veterans Affairs St. Louis Health Care System (VASTLHCS) John Cochran (JC) Hospital in St. Louis, Missouri. Offerors shall submit an offer subject to Project Labor Agreement (PLA) requirements in accordance with RFO 22.5, Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects. Any PLA reached pursuant to the PLA requirements in the solicitation does not change the terms of the contract or provide for any price adjustment by the Government. Funds are fully available for this requirement. The project will be solicited as full and open (unrestricted). The requirements under this construction project include right sizing the VAs medical center by demolishing several deficient and underutilized buildings and then constructing multiple new modern and seismically compliant structures and facilities on the same, expanded site. The newly constructed facilities are incorporated into a master plan for future expansion and demolition of additional primary facilities. The new primary facilities will be acquired using the Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) delivery method which includes a Pre-Construction Services Phase. The Government will evaluate the performance capability of offerors in accordance with the criteria described in the solicitation resulting in a single award under the best value continuum using the trade-off process in accordance with RFO 15.103-1 to the responsible offeror whose proposal the source selection authority determines conforms to the solicitation, is fair and reasonable, and offers the best overall value to the government, considering non-priced factors described in the solicitation and price. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236220, (Commercial and Institutional Building Construction), with a small business size standard of $45 million in average annual receipts. The estimated construction magnitude is over $1,000,000,000. The estimated performance period for the pre-construction services phase is 820 calendar days from Notice to Proceed (NTP).Interested offerors must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM). If the offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity must have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. title: Enterprise Inbound Email Retention and Forensic Analysis Solution
description: NOTICE UPDATE � NOVEMBER 18, 2026 The Government has updated this Sources Sought Notice to clarify the requirements in Sections 1, 2.A, and 2.C regarding downstream email delivery, Cisco IronPort integration, and the secure handling of potentially malicious emails. All other requirements remain unchanged. The response deadline remains November 25, 2026, at 3:00 PM Eastern Time. Enterprise Inbound Email Retention and Forensic Analysis Solution Sources Sought Notice / Request for Information (RFI) This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) for market research purposes only. This notice is issued solely for information and acquisition planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP), or a commitment to issue a solicitation in the future. The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) does not obligate itself to contract for any supply or service as a result of this notice. The Government is not currently seeking quotations or proposals and will not accept unsolicited quotations. The purpose of this notice is to identify potential vendors and commercially available solutions capable of meeting the IRS's enterprise email retention, search, and forensic analysis requirements. 1. BACKGROUND The Department of the Treasury, Internal Revenue Service (IRS), is seeking information on existing Commercial-Off-the-Shelf (COTS) solutions capable of providing enterprise-wide inbound email visibility, retention, centralized search, and forensic analysis capabilities for both legitimate (clean) and malicious emails. The IRS currently utilizes Cisco IronPort email security infrastructure and an existing Blind Carbon Copy (BCC) method to receive and retain copies of inbound email messages. The IRS is seeking a solution that can integrate with this existing infrastructure and preserve complete, unaltered copies of inbound emails, including message headers, content, metadata, and attachments. The IRS requires an enterprise-level solution that operates independently of individual Microsoft Outlook clients and does not rely on Outlook add-ons, plug-ins, or client-side software for enterprise email collection, retention, search, and forensic analysis. The proposed solution is not intended to perform downstream email delivery to Microsoft Exchange. Its primary function is to receive and securely retain inbound email copies for centralized search and forensic analysis. Interested vendors should identify any dependencies on downstream email systems associated with their proposed solutions. The IRS is interested in commercially available on-premises, virtual, cloud-based, or hybrid solutions. The Government is also interested in alternative technical approaches that can provide equivalent capabilities while meeting applicable federal security and operational requirements. The IRS does not have a predefined solution or architecture and welcomes information on commercially available products capable of meeting its operational needs. The results of this market research will assist the Government in identifying potential sources, assessing available commercial capabilities, and determining an appropriate acquisition strategy. The IRS anticipates a target implementation date of June 2027. Interested vendors should identify their estimated delivery and implementation timelines. 2. TECHNICAL CAPABILITIES Interested vendors are requested to describe their ability to meet the following anticipated technical and operational capabilities. Vendors should identify any capabilities that cannot be met or would require additional configuration, integration, or development. The Government welcomes information on alternative approaches that achieve equivalent operational outcomes. A. Cisco IronPort Integration and Email Collection Support integration with Cisco IronPort to receive and retain complete, unaltered copies of inbound email messages made available through the existing BCC method, including legitimate (clean) and potentially malicious emails, or an alternative collection method that provides equivalent functionality. Vendors should identify any collection limitations or integration dependencies associated with their proposed solutions. Preserve original message headers, content, metadata, and attachments for forensic investigations. Provide enterprise-wide email collection independent of Microsoft Outlook add-ons, plug-ins, or client-side applications. Identify any additional infrastructure, software, or configuration required for integration. B. Enterprise Email Volume and Retention The solution should be capable of supporting the following estimated email volumes: Up to approximately 1 million inbound emails per day. Peak email volume of approximately 150,000 emails per hour. Approximately 22 TB of inbound email data per month. Configurable retention periods ranging from 30 to 180 days for both legitimate and malicious emails. Vendors should describe the scalability, storage architecture, and performance capabilities of their proposed solutions. C. Email Search and Forensic Analysis Provide centralized search and investigation capabilities for both legitimate and malicious inbound email messages. Allow authorized analysts to search, retrieve, and review complete email messages, including headers, metadata, and attachments. Describe the solution's capabilities for identifying and classifying potentially malicious email messages, including any integration with existing email security tools. Describe available quarantine or equivalent isolation capabilities, whether provided directly by the solution or through integration with existing security infrastructure. Allow authorized analysts to view and download attachments for forensic investigations. Maintain message integrity throughout the retention and investigation process. Describe how the proposed solution securely receives, processes, retains, and supports forensic analysis of potentially malicious email messages and attachments while maintaining message integrity and protecting the system from malicious content. D. Third-Party Integration Support integration with Splunk for forwarding system logs, events, and email metadata. Support integration with Splunk SOAR for investigation and response automation. Provide APIs or equivalent interfaces for integration with additional security tools and automated workflows. E. Administration and System Management Provide secure command-line interface (CLI) access or equivalent administrative capabilities. Support high availability, redundancy, and automatic failover. Provide centralized system configuration, administration, and monitoring. For physical on-premises appliances, support IPMI or equivalent out-of-band hardware management. F. Security and Federal Compliance The solution must be capable of supporting applicable federal cybersecurity and audit requirements, including: IPv6 compatibility. Applicable FIPS 140-2 or FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic modules. Encryption of data at rest and in transit. Role-based access control (RBAC). Audit logging and monitoring. Configurable security warning banners. Secure input validation. Secure remote configuration backups. Active Directory integration, including LDAP and SAML-based authentication, as applicable. For cloud-based solutions, vendors shall identify their FedRAMP authorization status, authorization level, and any limitations or additional requirements associated with federal deployment. Vendors shall also identify the country of product development, hosting locations, data storage locations, and any applicable federal security or supply-chain considerations. G. Technical Support and Maintenance Provide information regarding 24x7 technical support availability. Identify whether technical support can be provided by U.S.-citizen personnel. title: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Marshalling Services - Yuma, AZ
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Marshalling Services 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required on or about January 1, 2027 � December 31, 2030 in Yuma, AZ. Interested parties must be located within 50 miles of the Yuma, AZ area. The vendor must be the owner or legal lessee of the facility. Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. Encourage maximum participation by offering a range of non-government affiliated services (retail financing, aftermarket warranties, vehicle enhancement etc.). Store, service and remarket of electric vehicles to include any necessary charging infrastructure. Transport vehicles to and from vendor locations. Prepare vehicles for public inspection and final sales/disposition, including services such as reconditioning, maintenance and repair, as well as equipment removal/disposal, and license plate & government credit card disposal and tracking. Offer industry-aligned services for customers to perform vehicle test drives. Provide state-of-the-art technology that will improve customer experience including enhanced condition reporting, 360� views, video, high-definition photography, etc. Conduct a full and open competitive sales process, including public inspection periods for all vehicles, and any related sale services for exchange/sale property. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage, and release of vehicles from time of receipt until final removal. Manage the logistics of vehicle transportation to bring vehicles to sale. Prepare vehicles for sale, to include vehicle equipment removal/disposal, reconditioning, and repairs. Work with local government entities to facilitate any inspections, documentation, and any other actions required to complete transactions in local markets. Perform electronic inventory management, vehicle inspection, complete condition reporting for vehicles. Offer recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, local market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Provide customer service to buyers in global markets. Create and execute marketing campaigns for local markets. Offer an internet sales platform with the potential to reach a global audience. Collect proceeds from vehicle sales and if necessary, convert to U.S. dollars. Marshalling only site tasks include, but are not limited to: Transport or resource/transportation of vehicles to and from vendor location (e.g., customer location, OEM dealership, offsite repair facility). Inspect vehicles upon delivery for various factors including but not limited to any damage to the vehicle, all components of the vehicle are accounted for (e.g., keys, floor mats, etc.), and missing equipment. Perform telematics device installation and/or activation on all new vehicles prior to releasing the vehicle to the customer. Validate new vehicles and options to vehicle order information provided by GSA. Perform pre-delivery inspections (PDI) in accordance with the manufacturer�s standards. Prepare new vehicles for customer receipt. Provide driver education for customers including vehicle operation, unique features, infotainment settings, etc. Offer specialized expertise and support on Electric Vehicle management, operation and charging infrastructure. Charge battery-powered vehicles. Maintain all vehicle fuel and charge levels as prescribed in the Statement of Work by GSA. Perform custodial and sales preparation services to facilitate auction house sales of GSA exchange lease vehicles. Process and manage all required vehicle shipment and delivery documentation. Manage scheduled vehicle appointments and ensure accurate vehicle exchanges. Perform all necessary tasks associated with confirming vehicle assignment and termination to and from the customer as prescribed by GSA. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to GSA Fleet and customer agencies throughout the marshalling process to ensure a seamless and transparent delivery and exchange process. Fulfill proper disposal of old/expired plates both front and back as prescribed by GSA. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage and inventory control of vehicles, license plates, credit cards and other assets from time of receipt until final removal. Scale charging capabilities to meet the needs of increasing electric vehicle adoption. 2.0 Background GSA Fleet provides a full-service fleet management program providing transportation solutions to partner agencies worldwide across the U.S. Federal government. It maintains a diverse fleet of over 250,000 vehicles, including light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, to include sedans, SUVs, vans, trucks, buses, ambulances, and law enforcement vehicles. Vehicles range from gasoline and diesel fueled vehicles to alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs), such as electric vehicles (EVs) to low-speed electric vehicles (LSEV�s) and non-powered vehicles and trailers. Nationally, GSA Fleet orders and receives on average 30,000+ vehicles from suppliers annually. As GSA Fleet is responsible for the disposition of its vehicles, it then remarkets and sells the used vehicles across the United States and its territories, Japan, and Europe. Its vehicles are sold under the exchange/sale authority of 41 CFR 102-39. This authority aims to expedite the disposal process and maximize proceeds in the most cost-effective manner to the U.S. taxpayer. To achieve this objective, GSA Fleet currently sells its used vehicles via live and online auctions worldwide, leveraging its contracts with commercial vendors to carry out all auction-related services. These auctions must adhere to all legal and regulatory requirements. They must also be open to the general public and provide an equal opportunity for individuals, businesses, government entities, and other organizations to take part in a zero-fee, fully open, and competitive sales process. To facilitate this process, GSA Fleet employs its vehicle remarketing specialists, who are warranted sales contracting officers and experts in the sales of its vehicles, to work with its vendors to approve repairs, pricing, as well as carry out and approve each sale to maximize net proceeds. All responsible sources may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or submit proposals, quotations or capability statements. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all proposals received within 45 days (30 days if award is issued under an existing Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) after date of publication of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Based upon market research, the Government is not using the policies contained in FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services, in its solicitation for the described supplies or services. However, interested persons may identify to the contracting officer their interest and capability to satisfy the Government's requirement with a commercial product within 15 days of this notice.

title: Pilot Training Transformation Device Support Services IV (PTT DSS IV)
description: The purpose of this requirement is to maintain and support PTT device solutions based on state- of-the-art commercial simulation environments, hardware solutions for the cockpit simulation environment, and ancillary software elements.The Contractor shall provide all services and equipment necessary to install, maintain, and support new and existing PTT devices. Devices currently fit into the following classifications: common Immersive Training Device (cITD), enhanced Immersive Training Devices (eITD), and Helicopter Immersive Training Device (HITD). Any new classifications will need to be defined and evaluated prior to inclusion in this scope. The Contractor shall support 142 ITDs and up to 17 Instructor Operating Stations (IOS) at the following locations: Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Randolph, TX; Columbus Air Force Base (AFB), MS; Laughlin AFB, TX; Vance AFB, OK, Sheppard AFB, TX; and Fort Rucker, AL. The Government has the right to modify the quantity of devices/locations pending contract modification and funding. The Contractor shall maintain a common software interface to integrate current and future PTT software and hardware components as required by program goals, hardware solutions for the cockpit simulation environment, and on-premises network and data architecture hardware and support, as appropriate for deployed training systems.

title: Modernize Regenerative Thermal Oxidizer (RTO)
description: SEEKING SOURCES ONLY - The Bureau of Engraving and Printing (BEP) Western Currency Facility (WCF) is located at 9000 Blue Mound Road, Fort Worth, TX, 76131. Construction began on the WCF in 1987 and was completed in 1989. The Modernized Regenerative Thermal Oxidizer (RTO) is an air pollution control device that is required by the NSR (New Source Review) Air Permit issued by the TCEQ (Texas Commission on Environmental Quality) to treat Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC) emissions from Plate Printing presses (14), Offset presses (4), and Rotary Screen presses (4). The existing RTO was commissioned in 2010 to control VOC emissions from Plate Printing. In 2021, the Offset presses were added to the RTO system. The existing conveyance system, which currently includes ducting from each press to the roof, nine (9) roof fans, and a 48" main duct on the roof, has been in place since the facility was built in the early 90s. The system has been cobbled together as presses were added in Plate Printing, which originally only housed four (4) presses, without consideration for the wholistic efficiency of the system. It is a requirement of the Clean Air Act, EPA regulations, and the WCF air permits, that an air pollution control device associated with a "facility" (equipment or area that is emitting air pollutants as defined by EPA) must be maintained in good condition and operated properly while the attached "facilities" operate. This design/build project shall replace the RTO and the associated exhaust ventilation system: a new RTO with a modern control panel including safe PLCs and lower working voltage, a properly designed exhaust ventilation system that self-optimizes with feedback from modern performance-monitoring systems, properly sized roof fans, accessibility to clean ducting where needed, and increased voe capture efficiency to better exhaust printing areas while allowing the RTO to operate using less supplemental fuel. The new system shall also incorporate features to decrease the amount of ink and oils that get conveyed into the exhaust ventilation system causing air flow issues and damaging ducting, fans, and other system components. Natural gas usage of the new RTO shall be metered and integrated into the BEP Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition (SCADA) system. In 2025, the existing RTO underwent several upgrades including the installation of a new, modern control panel to address obsolete components and increasingly difficult troubleshooting. This project shall set the Western Currency Facility (WCF) up for success in providing operational redundancy alongside the newly overhauled RTO that is currently operating at the facility. The entire voe exhaust ventilation system shall feed into one of two RTOs (existing or new) with the capability to divert process flow from one RTO to the other in the event one RTO shuts down for any reason. This redundancy shall enable production to continue operating while the root cause of the issue is addressed.

description: This is a solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 67100PR270000133 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for monthly potable-water sampling and laboratory testing services at U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Training Center (TRACEN) Cape May, 1 Munro Avenue, Cape May, NJ 08204. Prices shall be firm-fixed-price and all-inclusive; (3) A technical capability narrative demonstrating the offeror�s capability and management approach to meet all Statement of Work (SOW) requirements. At a minimum, address sampling coordination and collection procedures; chain-of-custody, preservation, transportation, and field-measurement procedures; laboratory analytical capability and ability to use the SOW-required analytical methods; timely electronic reporting and immediate-notification procedures; proposed personnel and equipment; and ability to comply with USCG facility-access, safety, identification, and security requirements; (4) Current evidence of New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) laboratory certification applicable to the required testing. If the offeror will use a subcontract laboratory, identify the laboratory and provide its applicable NJDEP certification; (5) At least two, but no more than three, recent and relevant past-performance references for comparable potable-water, drinking-water, wastewater, environmental sampling, or laboratory-analysis services performed within the past five years. For each reference, provide customer name; contract or project title; brief description of work performed; dollar value; period and place of performance; customer point of contact name, title, telephone number, and email address; and a brief explanation of relevance to this requirement; and (6) Acknowledgment of all solicitation amendments and a statement identifying any exceptions to solicitation terms and conditions. PERIOD FOR ACCEPTANCE OF QUOTATIONS The offeror agrees to hold the prices in its quotation firm for 60 calendar days from the date specified for receipt of quotations. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT USCG TRACEN Cape May requires a qualified contractor to provide all labor, supervision, equipment, sample containers, preservatives, transportation, laboratory analysis, and documentation necessary to conduct monthly potable-water sampling and laboratory testing. The Contractor shall collect potable-water samples from the first accessible potable-water sampling point downstream of the TRACEN Cape May water tower, or from another sampling location designated by the Government Technical Representative (GTR). Required testing includes total coliform, Escherichia coli (E. coli), free available chlorine residual, pH, turbidity, and total trihalomethanes (TTHMs). The Contractor shall use an NJDEP-certified laboratory for all required laboratory analyses. The Contractor shall coordinate each monthly sampling event with the GTR at least five business days in advance, unless otherwise agreed. The Contractor shall submit the required laboratory report and chain-of-custody documentation within 21 calendar days after sample collection. The Contractor shall notify the GTR by telephone and email within one business day after receipt of any result indicating E. coli detection or any result identified by the laboratory as requiring immediate notification or corrective action. For questions regarding visitor access, contact the designated Government POC.
