description: Amendment #1 � November 18, 2026 � Response Deadline Clarification Thank you for your interest and assistance in providing industry input on the draft Statement of Work, commercial availability of the contemplated services, customary industry practices, and alternative approaches to meeting the Government�s needs. The purpose of this amendment is to clarify that the final response deadline for RFI 75N94027R00005-RFI is Wednesday, November 25, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time. To support acquisition planning, we would appreciate receiving feedback by Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time, where feasible. Early submission is encouraged but is not required. Initial responses and supplemental information may be submitted through the final November 25 deadline. This clarification supersedes the November 19 deadline stated in the original RFI attachment. Submission instructions remain unchanged. Request for Information Request for Information No. 75N94027R00005-RFI Title NIMHD Division of Intramural Research Population Health and Clinical Research Type Research and Development (R&D) RFI Anticipated NAICS Code 541715 � Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) Response Date 4:00PM (Eastern) Wednesday, November 25, 2026 Primary Point of Contact Edwin Osorio, Contract Specialist � edwin.osorio@nih.gov Secondary Point of Contact Lisa Schaupp, Contracting Officer � lisa.schaupp@nih.gov Description This is a Request for Information (RFI) for Research and Development (R&D) open to all interested organizations, regardless of business size. This is NOT a solicitation for capability statements, proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose is to obtain industry input on the attached draft Statement of Work (SOW), the commercial availability of the contemplated services, customary industry practices, and alternative approaches to meeting the Government�s needs. This RFI is for market research and planning purposes only. The Government has not made a final determination regarding commerciality, acquisition strategy, task order pricing arrangements, or small business set-aside status. A solicitation may be issued later under a separate announcement; this RFI does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. Related notice: Small Business Sources Sought No. 75N94027R00005, published November 10, 2026. This separate RFI seeks industry feedback on the draft SOW and commercial availability; formal capability statements are not required. This RFI does not amend the separate Sources Sought notice or its response instructions. Background and Project Requirements The National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities (NIMHD), Division of Intramural Research (DIR), within the National Institutes of Health (NIH), seeks input on R&D social and behavioral sciences research services supporting population health and clinical research to understand and reduce health disparities in the United States. The contemplated effort encompasses the development, conduct, coordination, monitoring, analysis, and completion of multiple research studies through an Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. Study designs may include population-based cross-sectional surveys; epidemiological studies, including longitudinal cohort and case-control studies; clinical trials; community-based intervention studies; simulation modeling; and qualitative research, including observations, interviews, and focus groups. As described in the draft SOW, potential services include project management; research site and subcontract management; access to investigators, laboratories, facilities, equipment, and qualified personnel; participant recruitment and retention; community engagement; protocol development and implementation; regulatory and human-subjects protection support; site and safety monitoring; data collection, management, and statistical analysis; training; information security; and transition of research resources and data at contract completion. Individual task orders may differ in research design, populations, sites, duration, and complexity. For context, the related Sources Sought requested experience managing 3�6 studies annually, studies involving approximately 100�10,000 participants, and studies lasting from a few months to several years. These are experience ranges in that notice, not guaranteed task order quantities or established workload commitments. Respondents should identify assumptions affecting their feedback. Anticipated Award Date and Period of Performance The Government anticipates award of an IDIQ contract approximately in September 2027. Specific research activities and task order performance periods would be identified in individual task orders. Anticipated IDIQ ordering period Approximately five years Draft Statement of Work Feedback Provide comments or recommendations identifying the applicable SOW section or numbered item. Address unclear requirements, implementation challenges, opportunities to improve performance outcomes, and alternative or commercially available approaches. Identify requirements that may unnecessarily limit participation, including small business participation, and suggest practical revisions. Respondents may address all or selected portions of the draft SOW. Commercial Availability of Services The Government seeks evidence concerning whether the contemplated services, in whole or in part, are available in the commercial marketplace or could be met through customary commercial approaches. Please address the questions below to the extent relevant, distinguishing existing offerings from proposed study-specific development. Identify applicable SOW sections and provide nonproprietary supporting information where available. 1. Comparable commercial services. Which services or combinations of services described in the draft SOW are offered and sold to nongovernmental customers? Describe comparable tasks or outcomes, customer types, and similarities and differences in scope, scale, study complexity, and integration. Public descriptions, service literature, or nonproprietary examples may be provided; do not disclose confidential customer information. 2. Commercial sales and terms. For those services, describe whether and how they are offered and sold competitively, the frequency and extent of commercial sales, and customary commercial terms and conditions. Identify public sources or other nonproprietary information supporting the response. Distinguish experience serving Government customers from evidence of commercial-market sales. 3. Customary pricing practices. Describe customary pricing methods for specific tasks or outcomes, including established catalog or market prices where available, units of sale, and how prices can be substantiated. Identify typical payment arrangements and relevant commercial terms. Describe practices rather than submitting a binding quotation or a detailed cost proposal. 4. Customization and integration. Identify which SOW elements can be met through existing commercial services, which require customary tailoring, and which require specialized development or integration beyond customary practice. Explain the nature, extent, and principal cost or schedule drivers of any differences, including protocol-specific work, site coordination, data integration, security, or transition requirements. 5. Alternative approaches. Could the Government�s needs be met more effectively by restating requirements, using commercial service packages, or acquiring separable portions commercially? Describe feasible alternatives, dependencies, and potential effects on research continuity, oversight, performance, cost, schedule, and small business participation. 6. Pricing arrangements and research uncertainty. Identify portions suitable for firm-fixed-price arrangements and the conditions needed to define tasks,

description: Synopsis: This is a Small Business Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified small business sources to perform a potential requirement; (2) whether they are small businesses; 8(a) small businesses, service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses; veteran-owned small businesses; women-owned small businesses; HUBZone small businesses; or small disadvantaged businesses; and (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification system (NAICS) code for the potential acquisition. Your responses to the information requested will assist the government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a small business set aside is possible. An organization that is not considered a small business under the applicable NAICS code should not submit a response to this notice. The requirement is assigned a code of 541715 in the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS), and the small business size standard for such requirements is 1,000 employees or less. This notice is issued for market research purposes to assess potential small business sources, industry practices, and the availability of commercial services. The Government has not made a final determination regarding acquisition strategy, contract type, commerciality, or small business set-aside status. Respondents should identify whether they can perform the requirement as a prime contractor, including through existing teaming arrangements or qualified subcontractors, and distinguish their own capabilities from those of proposed team members. Background: The National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities (NIMHD) conducts and supports research and training programs to advance knowledge and understanding of health disparities, identify mechanisms to improve minority health and reduce health disparities, and develop effective interventions in community and clinical settings. NIMHD is the lead organization at the National Institutes of Health (NIH) for planning, reviewing, coordinating, and evaluating minority health and health disparities research activities. NIMHD also promotes workforce development, supports research capacity at less-resourced institutions that train students in research careers, serves populations experiencing health disparities, supports participation in clinical research, and promotes information dissemination through regular communications, public education outreach, and scientific presentations. The President�s Executive Order (EO) 14212 Establishing the President�s Make America Healthy Again Commission aims to improve the health of Americans. As described in the EO, escalating burden of chronic diseases poses significant challenges in the United States. These conditions contribute to rising health costs, reduced workforce productivity, and stagnant life expectancies across the country, both in adults and children. NIH defines a health disparity as a measurable difference in health that exists between specific population groups. This is a rigorously derived and data-driven determination operationalized by quantifiable metrics, rather than a statement of attribution. It is a scientific starting point that identifies where health outcomes diverge, not a predetermined conclusion about why. Scientific investigations to identify or understand the root causes are separate and distinct scientific questions, which are necessarily multifaceted and complex. NIH funded research is interested in those health disparities that are modifiable or actionable to improve the health of all population groups. Health disparities may be observed in the risks, prevalence, or problems resulting from specific behaviors, as well as the incidence, prevalence, and mortality from conditions, diseases, and/or disorders. To fulfill the NIH mission of seeking fundamental knowledge about the nature and behaviors of individuals as living systems, and the statutory purpose of NIMHD, to conduct research to understand and reduce health disparities, NIMHD Division of Intramural Research (DIR) conducts population health research to understand how health outcomes vary across populations, identify multilevel modifiable factors that drive these disparities, and develop, test, and evaluate clinical and population-based interventions to reduce these disparities. NIMHD DIR requires contractor assistance to provide R&D social and behavioral sciences research services to support NIMHD DIR in conducting population health and clinical research to understand and reduce health disparities in the United States. The Government anticipates that individual task orders may involve differing research designs, study populations, sites, durations, and levels of complexity. Interested firms should explain their ability to mobilize qualified personnel and research resources for multiple concurrent studies as requirements arise. NIMHD is seeking small businesses capable of designing, conducting and overseeing the clinical, scientific, and technical aspects of investigations into health disparities across populations, to identify modifiable risk and protective factors associated with these disparities, and develop and test interventions to reduce these disparities. Study designs to be used may include, but are not limited to: Population-based cross-sectional surveys; Epidemiological studies (e.g., longitudinal cohort study, case-control studies); Clinical trials; Community-based intervention studies; Simulation modeling; and Qualitative research methods (e.g., direct observations, in-depth interviews, focus groups discussions). Independently and not as an agent of the Government, the Contractor shall furnish all necessary services, qualified personnel, material, equipment, and facilities not otherwise provided by the Government to successfully perform the requirements stated below. Specifically, the Contractor shall, as required by individual task orders, perform the following technical requirements summarized below that also are included in the attached Draft Statement of Work (SOW), including but not limited to: Provide personnel, facilities, and other services necessary to maintain and coordinate multiple health disparities research studies funded through task orders under this Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. Provide overall project management and coordination of activities performed under individual task orders, including development and maintenance of project plans, schedules, milestones, coordination of participating research sites and subcontractors, monitoring of performance, identification and resolution of project risks and issues, and preparation of progress reports as specified in the applicable task order. Conduct research studies through qualified organizations, as specified in individual task orders, and receiving consent from the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR) and Contracting Officer (CO). This includes (but is not limited to) implementation of protocols; population health and clinical research site monitoring; regulatory compliance assurance; and analyses of data from clinical, laboratory, population and epidemiologic studies. Provide and manage participating population health research and clinical trial sites, investigators, laboratories, and other research resources necessary to conduct studies, directly or through qualified subcontractors. The Contractor shall draft, negotiate, execute, administer, monitor, renew and/or modify as necessary, subject to subcontractor's satisfactory past performance, and with the consent of the CO, subcontracts with domestic population health studies, clinical research sites and laboratories, and provide support for these population health studies, clinical research site and laboratories. title: France – Road transport services – 26SERV12 - Accord cadre à bons de commande pour les prestations de transport d'oeuvres et objets d'art pour les besoins de la Métropole Toulon Provence Méditerranée
description: Dans le cadre de sa politique culturelle, la Métropole Toulon Provence Méditerranée poursuit une politique d'attractivité territoriale en vue d'assurer un développement dynamique et durable et assume à ce titre la gestion en régie directe d'équipements culturels dans le domaine des arts visuels qui contribuent à son rayonnement au niveau national et international et dispose d'une collection d'oeuvres et objets d'art (art contemporain, photographie, sculptures). La présente consultation porte sur les besoins de la Métropole Toulon Provence Méditerranée en matière de prestations de transport d'oeuvres et objets d'art et activités connexes. Ces besoins concernent les oeuvres et objets d'art empruntés ou prêtés en France ou à l'étranger auprès d'acteurs publics et/ou privés (musées, institutions culturelles, galeries, collectionneurs...) pour la réalisation d'expositions temporaires ou dans le cadre de mouvements d'oeuvres. Ces prestations comprennent : - l'emballage des oeuvres et objets d'art avec étiquetage (du simple tamponnage à la fabrication et à la mise en caisse) aller/retour ; - les formalités « Beaux-arts » et douanières, - le transport des oeuvres et objets d'art par tout moyen (transport routier, aérien, maritime, fluvial ferroviaire) : l'acheminement depuis le ou les lieux d'enlèvement désignés (en France ou à l'étranger) vers les lieux de livraison désignés (en France ou à l'étranger) - les manutentions et le bardage (à savoir toutes formes de manutention manuelle ou mécanique pour déplacer et installer les oeuvres et objets d'art) à l'aller (avec une possible répartition dans les espaces des lieux désignés) et au retour, - le déballage des oeuvres et objets d'art à l'aller et au retour, - l'entreposage des oeuvres et objets d'art - des prestations complémentaires - le suivi et la coordination de ces différentes opérations.

title: Request for Information (RFI) for Aerial Targets Branch (EBAY) Air Force Aerial Target Solutions
description: Issued pursuant to Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) FAR 15.101(c) and RFO FAR Part 10 solely for information, market research, and planning purposes. This market survey is conducted by the Aerial Targets Program Office (AFLCMC/EBAY) under the Air Force Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Weapons (AFPAE/WP) to obtain industry capabilities, rough order of magnitude (ROM) information, and data needed to support commercial product/service, non-developmental item (NDI), and small business determinations under RFO FAR 10.001(f), and to inform acquisition planning. Per Title 10, U.S. Code �4172, major munitions and missile programs must demonstrate lethality against appropriate, threat-representative targets prior to full-rate production. The Aerial Targets mission is to provide target aircraft that replicate threat systems, including performance, signatures, and countermeasures of adversary aircraft. The objective of this RFI is to identify a range of solutions to populate a family for systems needed throughout the spectrum of missions in Defensive and Offensive Counter Air capabilities. These solutions may represent the full range of airborne threats, spanning from inexpensive �hobby drones� to the most advance adversary fighter and large-scale aircraft. This RFI is intended to: Identify commercially available or near-term solutions Understand industry capabilities and innovative approaches Inform future acquisition strategies and budgetary requirements and assist the agency in making commerciality, NDI, and small business set-aside determinations See attached RFI and Question and Answer documents and for additional details. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ In accordance with Section 10 of the attached RFI, attached are the final Questions and Answers posted on 11 SEPTEMBER 2026. ALL FINAL RESPONSES ARE DUE BY 28 SEPTEMBER 2026 @ 1600 CENTRAL.

This procurement is unrestricted. The attached list of NSNs are the items that have been identified for this current action. It is the Government�s intent to use a letter solicitation format to the sole source Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM); therefore, if any non-OEM source is interested in any of the NSNs, please notify the Contracting Officer prior to the synopsis closing date. For registration procedures and information please visit the World Wide Web at https://www.sam.gov. A paper copy of the solicitation will not be available to requestors. title: U.S. Army National Guard Culinary Assessment and G4G Training at Devils Lake ND
description: Seeking a highly qualified vendor with the prerequisite knowledge, skills and proven (demonstrated) abilities to provide a two-phase culinary operations assessment and customized training engagement in support of the Supernatural Eats LLC and the U.S. Army National Guard (231 QMT Platoon) operations in Devils Lake, North Dakota. The engagement shall evaluate existing food service operations, identify opportunities for improvement, and provide practical culinary training aligned with the facility's operational requirement and the U.S. Army Go for Green (G4G) food program initiative. Phase I of this requirement shall consist of a multi-day, projected at two days, on-site assessment conducted by a recognized by the culinary community Culinary Arts subject-matter expert (SME). Phase II of this new requirement shall consist of a CUSTOMIZED five day, executive chef instructor-led, hands-on culinary training program delivered on site for up to __X__ number Supernatural Eats, LLC and 231 QMT guardsman participants. The content of Phase II shall be informed by Phase I findings. This new requirement shall not include a culinary certification examination or issuance of any professional certification. In order to be considered as eligible for this new requirement, the vendor shall possess demonstrated, multi-year specialized institutional experience and technical capabilities directly aligned with the intent of up training all attendees in consistently preparing many hundreds of G4G meals that retain highest quality food preparation for the duration of the line service at the Camp Grafton Training Center (CGTC) Dining Facility (DFAC). Interested vendors SHALL submit documentation that the proposed culinary training team has demonstrated past performance expertise in conducting on-site needs assessments at military and institutional food service facilities, demonstrated experience is documented of the vendor's abilities at evaluating operational capabilities and constraints, and translating assessment findings into measurable training objectives, site specific curricula, and actionable operational outcomes. Failure to demonstrate these necessary culinary arts skill sets shall remove those vendors from further consideration for this specific new requirement. Once again, to reiterate, the NDARNG intent is to locate and validate all interested vendors who do have demonstrated and extensive, more than just a few, experience providing culinary assessment, workforce development, and training services to the United States Air Force, other branches of the United States Armed Forces, and the Department of War. NDARNG has a preferrence for locating vendors who have played an instrumental role in developing the culinary and operational standars associated with the Army Food Program, Go for Green (G4G) 2.0 initiative and furthermore a vendor that has conducted assessments and delivered training at military installations throughout the continental United States (CONUS) and outside the continental United States (OCONUS). NDARNG intends to develop a highly trained DFAC staff that shall be able to provide on a consistent, high volume meal preparation basis, quality G4G meals for students who travel from across the country and territories in order to receive training at our Engineering, Regional Training Institute (RTI). It is of utmost importance to NDARNG executive leadership that the vendor hired for this new requirement possesses the combination of culinary arts program development experience, familiarity with military food service environments, and can immediately gain the respect of all attendees because the vendor has an excellent reputation in these culinary arts assessment and training elements. Interested contractors shall submit BOTH their Phase I -- Culinary Operations Assessment documentation along with their Phase II -- Customized Culinary Training documentation, which shall be evaluated by the NDARNG food services team in order to determine whether the vendor is qualified to compete for this new culinary arts assessment and training requirement. Any interested vendors shall also provide their DELIVERABLES and REPORTING documentation to our office, as evidence that your company is highly qualified with many previous experiences in providing this type of highly specialized culinary arts assessment and training new requirement. At this stage of the contracting preaward process, there is no need for sharing your proposed total amount for this new requirement; however, if you should wish to provide your Rough Order Magnitude (ROM) pricing structure, please feel free to do so. In closing, one final request is made by our office. Please let us know within your submission whether your company is considered a Small Business or a Large Business under either NAICS 611519 or 611430. Thank you for your interest in this requirement, as demonstrated by your submission of a Sources Sought (RFI) Notice response that fully meets all of our noted mandatory elements as listed above.

title: Homeland Security and Innovation Center (HSIC) - Executive Education Seminar Services
description: HSIC, located at Joint Force Headquarters�Massachusetts, supports the National Guard by connecting senior-leader education with the evolving challenges of homeland security, emergency management, crisis leadership, and innovation. Its education mission includes General and Flag Officer Seminar (GFOS) and Leadership in Homeland Security (LHS) audiences. The seminars emphasize rigorous academic study, case-based analysis, facilitated discussion, critical thinking, and peer networking in a university setting. The curriculum should address National Guard roles in complex domestic response and intergovernmental coordination and, as appropriate to each seminar, emerging challenges such as artificial intelligence, cyber threats, small unmanned aircraft systems/counter-sUAS, and innovation. Inclusion and emphasis of these topics remain subject to HSIC/GOMO mission validation. The broader HSIC innovation/incubation mission does not automatically expand the scope of this seminar-services requirement. MARKET RESEARCH FEEDBACK REQUESTED Institutions are invited to comment on academic capability, delivery and pricing feasibility, and requirements that may unnecessarily constrain participation. Responses should identify the affected section, explain the practical or financial impact, and propose alternatives that preserve HSIC educational quality. Contracting will determine final response instructions. Academic institution and faculty qualifications: experience educating GOs or comparable senior executives; relevant faculty credentials; impact of tenured-Ph.D./ten-year criteria. GFOS and LHS differentiation: recommended objectives, topics, and approaches appropriate to each audience; capability to address AI, cyber, sUAS/cUAS, and innovation. Case-study pedagogy and research: existing course adaptation, case-study counts, original case development, guest speaker access, realistic research and approval timelines. Seminar capacity, location, and duration: in-person facilities for 65 plus support staff; viable course lengths; scheduling lead times; capacity for multiple annual iterations. Enrollment and pricing: ability to handle 40 Government-funded and up to 25 direct-pay seats; tuition-only versus standard bundled seminar pricing; minimum cohort sizes. Intellectual property: rights and restrictions for pre-existing materials versus Government-funded new case studies; possible licensing and reuse models. Participation barriers: federal contracting, administrative requirements, location, security, teaming, and any provisions that materially affect willingness or ability to compete. TARGETED UNIVERSITY FEEDBACK QUESTIONS � ACADEMIC AND BUSINESS FEASIBILITY Which performance outcomes and academic quality indicators best demonstrate that an executive education program meets HSIC needs? Which specific faculty criteria, if any, would prevent your institution from competing, and what evidence of equivalent academic quality could you provide? What case-study-based instructional model would you propose, and how would HSIC verify the quality of learning? What enrollment, lead time, and annual frequency would make participation financially viable for your institution? How would your institution price standard bundled tuition, meals, books, and facilities compared with a tuition-only arrangement, if available? Which administrative or payment requirements (including direct-pay seats and federal contracting) would discourage a response, and what alternatives could address them? Based on this draft PWS, what specific requirements or business conditions would discourage your institution from competing? Would your institution be interested in competing? If not, what changes would materially affect that decision? SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS & INSTRUCTIONS Interested academic institutions who believe they have the capability to perform this requirement are invited to submit their feedback and Capability Statement. Please refer to the attached draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) (File: HSIC_PWS_Draft.docx) when compiling their responses. To be considered complete, the submission package MUST contain: 1. Administrative Profile (including UEI and CAGE Code) 2. Technical Capabilities Narrative 3. Comments on the 7 Market Research Feedback Areas 4. Direct Answers to the 8 Targeted University Feedback Questions Please ensure the email subject line reads: "Sources Sought Response: W912SV27SS0001 - HSIC Executive Education Seminar Services" Responses must be submitted via email to the following points of contact: Primary POC: Marc Kerrigan (marc.j.kerrigan.civ@army.mil) Alternative POC: Isao Hattori (isao.hattori.civ@army.mil) Please note that no phone calls or inquiries will be accepted or acknowledged regarding this market survey. description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), Patuxent River, MD intends to issue a modification to the existing Sustaining Engineering and Support (SES) IV Contract, N0001924C0005, on a sole source basis to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation (NGSC). The anticipated contract modification is for incorporation of highly specialized sustainment support of the Triton MQ-4C Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) unique to the Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF). Efforts will include, but not be limited to, generation of RAAF unique engineering test procedures, RAAF unique network configuration documentation, and RAAF unique engineering and technical reports, informed by currently performed sustainment activities. This contract modification is being pursued on a sole source basis under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204 (a)(l) as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 6.103-1, "Only One Responsible Source and No Other Type of Supplies or Services will Satisfy Agency Requirements." NGSC is the sole designer, developer, manufacturer, integrator, and producer of the MQ-4C Triton air vehicles and ground stations. Therefore, NGSC is the only source with the requisite knowledge of the Triton design, operation, and maintenance to successfully provide the necessary FSRs, engineering, systems integration, and sustainment support. Information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for or award a contract. No telephone inquiries will be accepted.

description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation in accordance with FAR Part 13. This is a simplified acquisition to establish a contract for a breath switch. description: The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the provision of Imagery Exploitation and Visualization Tools. title: Request for Information (RFI) for Aerial Targets Branch (EBAY) Air Force Aerial Target Solutions
description: Issued pursuant to Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) FAR 15.101(c) and RFO FAR Part 10 solely for information, market research, and planning purposes. This market survey is conducted by the Aerial Targets Program Office (AFLCMC/EBAY) under the Air Force Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Weapons (AFPAE/WP) to obtain industry capabilities, rough order of magnitude (ROM) information, and data needed to support commercial product/service, non-developmental item (NDI), and small business determinations under RFO FAR 10.001(f), and to inform acquisition planning. Per Title 10, U.S. Code �4172, major munitions and missile programs must demonstrate lethality against appropriate, threat-representative targets prior to full-rate production. The Aerial Targets mission is to provide target aircraft that replicate threat systems, including performance, signatures, and countermeasures of adversary aircraft. The objective of this RFI is to identify a range of solutions to populate a family for systems needed throughout the spectrum of missions in Defensive and Offensive Counter Air capabilities. These solutions may represent the full range of airborne threats, spanning from inexpensive �hobby drones� to the most advance adversary fighter and large-scale aircraft. This RFI is intended to: Identify commercially available or near-term solutions Understand industry capabilities and innovative approaches Inform future acquisition strategies and budgetary requirements and assist the agency in making commerciality, NDI, and small business set-aside determinations See attached RFI and Question and Answer documents and for additional details. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ In accordance with Section 10 of the attached RFI, attached are the final Questions and Answers posted on 11 SEPTEMBER 2026.
